title: Staff Platform Engineer
description:
Description:

Job Summary:

The Staff Platform Engineer sets the technical direction for the platform and solves infrastructure problems that span teams. The role stays hands-on — writing and reviewing infrastructure code and operating production systems — but most of its impact comes from shaping how the whole engineering organization builds, deploys, and runs software, without formal management authority. Staff engineers may also serve as a team's Tech Lead, a role that carries no change in title, band, or bonus.

Key Responsibilities:

Regularly audit and evaluate the platform's architecture, and lead the design and delivery of major
architectural changes across teams on an annual basis.
Write technical proposals for those changes and build agreement on them with product and engineering
stakeholders.
Set org-wide standards for infrastructure patterns, delivery practices, tooling, and technology choices.
Partner with Buyer and Cargo engineering leadership so the platform supports what their teams need to build
next.
Define observability, reliability, and incident standards, and take on the hardest production problems: systemic
bottlenecks, performance crises, and failures under heavy contention.
Plan and carry out large migrations, such as database moves, network re-architecture, and project
restructuring, without disrupting live auctions.
Own the platform's security, cost, and capacity strategy.
Mentor senior engineers and act as a force multiplier, influencing direction without formal authority.
Requirements:

Qualifications / Requirements:

Autonomy: Leads strategy — defines technical direction without day-to-day oversight.
Technical Depth: Visionary — deep expertise with the ability to see and shape the broader technical landscape.
Leadership Impact: Force multiplier and system architect — makes entire teams more effective.
Business Impact: Strategic — future-proofs systems and drives technical decisions that enable business growth.
Experience: 7-10+ years of professional engineering experience, with a demonstrated record of infrastructure or platform impact across teams.
Education: Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, related field, or equivalent practical experience.
Advanced study in Computer Science, Systems Engineering, or a related discipline (Master's or equivalent graduate-level work) is a strong differentiator at this level.

Technical Skills

Languages: Expert-level proficiency in TypeScript and strong proficiency in Go or Python.
Infrastructure as Code: Sets standards for infrastructure as code — state management, resource lifecycle, refactoring and aliasing, and reusable component design. Pulumi in TypeScript is a strong plus.
Cloud: GCP architecture expertise — designs for reliability, cost efficiency, and scale across GKE, Cloud Run, Cloud SQL, Pub/Sub, and BigQuery.
Networking: Network architecture expertise — multi-project VPC design, private service connectivity, load balancing, mTLS, and traffic management.
Databases: Deep expertise in operating MySQL, PostgreSQL, and distributed SQL — replication, connection pooling, schema evolution at scale, and zero-downtime migrations.
Observability: Designs and owns observability strategy — alerting, SLOs/SLAs, and distributed tracing.
Security: Understands security at the architecture level — auth patterns, secrets management, network security, IAM, and defending against abusive traffic.
Technical Fundamentals: Expert-level distributed systems knowledge — consensus, replication strategies, concurrency control under write contention, exactly-once semantics, and fault-tolerant design; OS and runtime internals relevant to performance (GC behavior, syscall overhead, context switching); systems design fluency — can decompose and reason about large-scale distributed architectures from first principles.

Nice to Have

Temporal or other durable workflow orchestration.
CockroachDB, PgBouncer, or large-scale database migration and replication.
Cloud Armor, WAF, or bot-mitigation experience.
Vertex AI or other ML serving infrastructure.
Experience architecting systems with heavy write contention, such as many users acting on the same records at once in bidding, inventory, or payments.

Physical Requirements:

Ability to remain seated or stationary for extended periods while working at a computer.
Frequent use of hands and fingers for typing, mouse use, and other computer-related tasks.
Ability to communicate effectively in person, by phone, and through electronic communication.
Ability to occasionally stand, walk, bend, reach, or move about the office.
Ability to occasionally lift and carry office equipment or materials up to 10–15 pounds.
Visual ability sufficient to read computer screens, documents, and other work-related materials.
Ability to perform the essential functions of the position with or without reasonable accommodation.

title: Senior Infrastructure Engineer — Secure Developer Platforms (Azure / VDI)
description:
Company Description

Oteemo is an industry-leading technology consulting firm at the forefront of AI-driven, cloud native, enterprise DevSecOps transformation. We build intelligent, automated, secure systems for organizations tackling their toughest technical and business challenges and we're pushing the boundaries of what AI, generative AI, and agentic systems can do in production, not just in theory. Join us and you'll work alongside recognized experts on cutting-edge projects that blend cloud native architecture, extreme automation, and AI/ML at the core. We foster a dynamic, inclusive, and collaborative culture built on continuous learning, where your ideas shape real outcomes for our clients. If you're passionate about building what's next in AI and cloud technology and want to do it with a team that sets the standard rather than follows it, Oteemo is where you belong.

Job Description

We're looking for a Senior Infrastructure Engineer to build a secure, self-service developer sandbox inside a regulated energy utility's Azure tenant. You'll deliver non-persistent, streamed desktops on Azure Virtual Desktop and Omnissa Horizon that rebuild clean at every log off, keep developers' work, and send all traffic through TLS-inspected egress while still booting in under a minute. You'll own the stack from landing zone to golden image.

Key Responsibilities:

Non-Persistent Desktops: Stand up pooled AVD and Omnissa Horizon (instant clone) desktops streamed over HTTPS 443; run the head-to-head POC that selects the platform; persist developer state with FSLogix or Dynamic Environment Manager and App Volumes.

Landing Zone & Inspected Egress: Build hub-and-spoke VNets segmented from production, with forced-tunnel egress through Azure Firewall Premium (TLS inspection, IDPS), private endpoints, and DNS; tune inspection so Git, package managers, GitHub Copilot, and AI/MCP endpoints keep working.

Golden Image & Endpoint Controls: Own the Azure Image Builder or Packer pipeline to Azure Compute Gallery (build, patch, CIS-harden, scan, publish); keep CarbonBlack App Control allow-lists and BeyondTrust EPM working across rebuilds.

Identity, Guardrails & Logging: Enforce guardrails as code with Azure Policy and Terraform or Bicep; wire a non-production identity tenant, per-project RBAC, and Key Vault; forward firewall, desktop, and provisioning logs to Sentinel or Splunk.

Self-Service, AI Agents & Handover: Build ephemeral resource templates with TTL and an orphaned-resource reaper; expose image pipelines so AXIOM AI agents can propose promotions that humans approve; deliver architecture, runbooks, and a support model.

Qualifications

Bachelor's degree in a related field (or equivalent practical experience).

8+ years in infrastructure or platform engineering, including 4+ years of hands-on Azure in an enterprise or regulated environment.

Virtual Desktop: Delivered at least one production AVD or Omnissa / VMware Horizon deployment, including non-persistent pools, image lifecycle, and FSLogix or DEM / App Volumes at scale.

Azure Networking: Deep experience with VNets, UDRs, Azure Firewall (Premium TLS inspection preferred), Private Link, DNS, and NSGs, including troubleshooting broken TLS chains.

IaC & Identity: Expert Terraform or Bicep run through CI/CD; Packer or Azure Image Builder; Entra ID, RBAC, PIM, managed identities, Key Vault, and Azure Policy.

Working knowledge of Windows 11 multi-session hardening and Linux for container workloads; clear writer who can get a design approved by a Cyber Risk reviewer.

Nice to Have / Preferred Qualifications:

Certifications: Azure: AZ-104, AZ-700, AZ-140, AZ-305; Terraform Associate; VCP-DTM.

Tuning CarbonBlack App Control, BeyondTrust EPM, CrowdStrike, or Defender for Endpoint for developer workloads.

Additional Information

We Value:

Drive: Passion and energy to implement quality technical solutions. Self-motivation and intellectual curiosity
Commitment to Quality: Passion to conceive and produce world-class solutions that drive real-world value for the customer
Customer Focus: Consultative approach to solving problems for customers. Expectations management.
Communication: Superior communication skills. Ability to clearly articulate problems, solutions, risks, rewards etc. (written and verbal)
Technical Skills: Love for technology. You have to be inherently passionate about technology.
Business Acumen: Technology ultimately is used to enable the business. We look for people who understand how the businesses can be enabled through their technical solutions

All your information will be kept confidential according to EEO guidelines.

title: Staff Forward Deployed Engineer, Platform
description:
Description:

About Us

eSimplicity is a modern digital services company that partners with government agencies to improve the lives and protect the well-being of all Americans, from veterans and service members to children, families, and seniors. Our engineers, designers, and strategists cut through complexity to create intuitive products and services that equip federal agencies with solutions to courageously transform today for a better tomorrow.

Purpose and Scope

We’re seeking a Staff Forward Deployed Engineer, Platform to join eSimplicity’s Rapid Innovation Center (the RIC). The Staff Forward Deployed Engineer, Platform works primarily with internal stakeholders, including program teams, growth teams, executives, business unit CTOs, security leaders, and engineering teams, to identify high-value operational and mission problems and shape the platform, DevOps, cloud, integration, and automation foundations needed to deliver working prototypes and MVPs from concept through validation.

As part of a small, high-trust team, this engineer is expected to take initiative, work effectively through ambiguity, and bring sound judgment to fast-moving technical challenges. The role requires ownership, adaptability, and close collaboration to help internal teams move quickly while establishing reliable developer workflows, secure cloud patterns, CI/CD practices, observability, infrastructure automation, and reusable platform foundations that can be adopted across the company.

The role may engage external customers when needed to understand mission context, validate assumptions, or support a program or pursuit, but its primary purpose is to help internal teams move faster and turn validated ideas into repeatable company capabilities.

This is a Staff-level, hands-on technical role for someone who can move fluidly across discovery, solution shaping, architecture, and implementation while partnering with product, program, security, and engineering leaders. This is an individual contributor role with technical leadership responsibilities; it does not include direct people-management responsibilities or ownership of companywide AI governance. Successful work is matured into repeatable patterns, reusable components, reference architectures, adoption guidance, and transition plans that other eSimplicity programs and capture teams can adopt.

Responsibilities

Partner with program teams, growth teams, executives, business unit CTOs, security leaders, engineering teams, and other internal stakeholders to identify high-value operational or mission problems, clarify needs, define success measures, and translate ambiguity into executable solution approaches.
Partner with product and design stakeholders to conduct interviews, discovery sessions, and workflow analysis, then translate those insights into user-centered concepts, interaction patterns, prototypes, and validation approaches for mission-aligned solutions.
Shape pragmatic solution approaches and contribute directly to architecture, code, integrations, demos, AI applications, data solutions, platform services, prototypes, and MVPs from discovery through validation and transition planning.
Make clear technical tradeoffs across speed, security, scalability, reuse, maintainability, cost, operational readiness, and mission value.
Design and integrate systems, APIs, data sources, cloud services, CI/CD pipelines, infrastructure-as-code, release automation, identity controls, observability, monitoring, and deployment automation using Agile, DevSecOps, DataOps, and AnalyticOps practices.
Build and evolve reusable platform capabilities, including services, APIs, developer workflows, CI/CD templates, infrastructure automation, environment patterns, data integration patterns, secure cloud patterns, and shared technical components that multiple programs and engineering teams can adopt.
Apply existing security, privacy, and responsible AI expectations appropriate to prototype or MVP maturity, including PII/PHI protection, access control, auditability, transparency, human oversight, and escalation of governance decisions to the appropriate company or program owners.
Mature successful work into reusable components, implementation patterns, reference architectures, adoption guidance, and transition plans for scaled development, sustainment, or reuse across programs and capture teams.
Enable adoption through workshops, whiteboarding sessions, onboarding materials, playbooks, technical reviews, and coaching that help internal teams understand, trust, and reuse RIC-built capabilities.
Mentor engineers, architects, and delivery teams by sharing patterns, reviewing solution approaches, and raising the technical bar across engagements.
Other duties as assigned.
Requirements:
A Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Information Systems, Engineering, Math, or a related scientific or technical discipline.
7+ years of hands-on software, data, platform, cloud, or AI engineering experience, with demonstrated ability to build solutions directly while influencing technical direction across more than one area such as discovery, solution architecture, stakeholder engagement, backlog shaping, or implementation planning.
Strong hands-on depth in platform engineering, DevOps, cloud infrastructure, CI/CD, automation, observability, identity, and secure integration patterns, with working fluency in adjacent areas such as full-stack engineering, data engineering, AI/ML engineering, or integration architecture as needed for various engagements.
Demonstrated record of taking ambiguous internal, program, or customer problems to working prototypes or MVPs quickly while maintaining sound technical judgment, security awareness, and delivery discipline.
Strong stakeholder-facing skills, including the ability to work directly with executives, program leaders, engineers, security stakeholders, capture teams, and, when needed, government customers.
Experience integrating multiple systems, APIs, data sources, cloud services, and modern AI technologies, including LLM and agentic approaches, in secure enterprise or government environments.
Experience designing and building secure solutions that handle PHI, PII, or other sensitive data, with working knowledge of privacy, authorization, governance, auditability, and responsible AI expectations.
Working knowledge of cloud services, infrastructure automation, CI/CD, build and release pipelines, identity, observability, monitoring, environment management, data integration, secure integration patterns, and reusable platform or developer-enablement capabilities.
Experience designing or operating observability practices for cloud or platform environments, including logging, metrics, tracing, dashboards, alerting, service health indicators, and operational feedback loops that improve reliability and supportability.
Excellent executive, technical, and written communication skills, including the ability to translate complex technical decisions into mission, business, delivery, and risk implications.
Experience leading work in Agile or SAFe environments, including backlog management, technical planning, delivery coordination, and use of Atlassian Jira/Confluence.
Ability to obtain and maintain a Public Trust and reside in the United States.

Preferred Qualifications

Federal, DoD, or health IT experience, especially experience influencing government stakeholders or delivering solutions in Medicare, Medicaid, healthcare, or Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services environments. GovCon experience is not required for an exceptional builder with strong stakeholder instincts.
Hands-on experience with platforms such as Databricks and Palantir, and experience designing, building, or operationalizing LLM and agentic AI applications such as MCP servers, agents, retrieval-based solutions, and governed AI workflows.
Prior forward-deployed engineering, technical consulting, solution architecture, platform engineering, or senior engineering experience, including translating prototypes into reusable components, reference architectures, and transition plans.
Experience mentoring engineers, shaping technical standards, reviewing architectures, and improving engineering quality across multiple teams or engagements.
Relevant certifications or advanced training in data platforms, cloud architecture, coding, AI/ML architecture, platform engineering, or applied AI delivery.

Working Environment:

eSimplicity supports a hybrid work environment operating within the Eastern time zone so we can work with and respond to our government clients. Expected hours are 9:00 AM to 5:00 PM Eastern unless otherwise directed by your manager.

Occasional travel for training and project meetings. It is estimated to be less than 5% per year.

title: Senior Scientist I, Cheminformatics
description:
Eikon Therapeutics is a new biopharmaceutical company employing revolutionary technology at the intersection of chemistry, engineering, computation, and biology to discover novel treatments for life-threatening diseases. Eikon's discovery platform is built on groundbreaking innovations from its founders (Nobel Prize, 2014), culminating in the creation of microscopes which enable real time, molecular-resolution measurements of protein movement in living cells, thereby unlocking otherwise intractable classes of proteins as drug targets.

Position

We seek a Senior Scientist with a demonstrated ability of successfully applying Cheminformatics and ML technologies to drive the discovery programs. You will collaborate closely with computational chemists, medicinal chemists, software engineers and machine learning experts to turn assay and structure-activity data into interpretable information for decision making. As an integral member of our Drug Discovery team, you will make a real and direct impact on accelerating the drug discovery process and ultimately benefiting patients.

About You

You're a cheminformatics expert who loves to solve difficult problems and are not discouraged by challenges. You have a passion for drug discovery and thrive in a fast-paced, dynamic environment. You are curious, love challenges, and enjoy pushing the edge of technology to solve important problems with creative solutions. You're collaborative by nature, resourceful, open-minded, data-driven, and can operate with a sense of urgency.

What You'll Do

Develop and apply cheminformatics data-mining algorithms for the analysis of molecular modeling, virtual screening, and structure-activity relationship (SAR) analysis.
Process and analyze chemical and biological datasets to evaluate properties such as drug-likeness, ADMET properties, dosing, etc.
Utilize molecular fingerprints, descriptors, and similarity metrics for compound clustering, classification, and regression.
Assist in development, maintenance, and monitoring of AI/ML models used for property prediction.
Optimize data pipelines for processing and storing chemical structures using cheminformatics toolkits (e.g., RDKit).
Collaborate with cross-functional teams to integrate computational approaches into curation and analysis workflows.
Maintain best practices in data integrity, reproducibility, and documentation of QSAR AI/ML models.
Provide guidance on the application of modern cheminformatics, ML/AI methods for library design (e.g. diversity, focused, fragment, DEL) and analyzing large datasets from HTS campaigns to building predictive models from them.
Routinely employ expert knowledge and analysis of SAR, physiochemical and ADMET properties.
Work alongside medicinal chemists to further triage emerging hits from HTS.
Collaborate closely with our data science team to integrate cutting edge AI/ML tools into our chemistry and drug discovery processes.

Qualifications

Ph.D. plus 5 years of relevant experience; or Master's plus 14 years of relevant experience; or Bachelor's plus 16 years of relevant experience.
Expertise in cheminformatics data analysis, data mining, and machine learning models to solve drug discovery problems.
Expertise with ligand-based design approaches, QSAR, multiparameter optimization to rationalize SAR and design novel molecules.
Expertise in scientific programming languages such as python, with experience using RDKit and other cheminformatic libraries and data analytics (Spotfire, DataWarrior, D360).
Experience in virtual screening, HTS triaging, hit calling, and diversity analysis.
Familiar with commercial platforms and ELN/registration systems (Schrödinger, OpenEye, MOE, Dotmatics, DataBricks, KNIME).
A track record of publications, patents and/or conference presentations in computational chemistry and/or drug discovery.
Excellent problem-solving abilities and the ability to work in a fast-paced, dynamic research environment.
Strong communication skills with the ability to convey complex scientific concepts to both technical and non-technical stakeholders.

At Eikon, employee compensation also includes bonus and equity compensation, in addition to several generous benefit programs, including:

401k plan with company matching
Medical (premiums covered by Eikon at 95%), dental and vision insurance (premiums covered by Eikon at 100%)
Mental health and wellness benefits
Weeklong summer and winter holiday shutdowns
Generous paid time off and holiday policies
Life/AD&D Insurance (premiums covered by Eikon at 100%) and optional supplemental employee-paid life/AD&D policies
Enhanced parental leave benefit
Daily subsidized lunch program when on-site

The expected salary range for this role is $178,000 to $215,250 depending on skills, competency, and the market demand for your expertise.

Eikon is proud to be an equal opportunity employer and will consider all qualified applicants for employment.

title: Senior DevOps Engineer I
description:
ABOUT ROCKET LAB

Rocket Lab is the end-to-end space company building rockets, spacecraft, and critical subsystems that keep the world connected, protected, expand humanity's reach to the Moon, Mars, and beyond. We move fast, build real hardware for meaningful missions, and make the impossible routine. Come shape the future with us.

SPACE SYSTEMS

At Rocket Lab, we're not just launching rockets — we're building the future of space. Our Space Systems team builds everything from complete spacecraft, precision payloads to the components and subsystems that allow them to thrive in space, like solar panels, flight software, star trackers, optical systems, separation systems, radios, and more.

Our Space Systems team has enabled more than 1,700 missions, ranging from interplanetary exploration, in-space manufacturing to national security and defense initiatives. The team has built spacecraft, payloads, and components for missions to the Moon and Mars, working with partners including NASA, the Space Development Agency, and the U.S. Space Force. Whether it's a single high-performance spacecraft, constellation, or the vertically integrated components that help them get to space — our world class Space Systems team is empowering some of the boldest and most ambitious space missions.

SENIOR DEVOPS ENGINEER I

Based out of Rocket Lab's site in Littleton, CO, we are looking to hire a Senior DevOps Engineer I. In this role you will build, operate, and improve the observability platform that gives our teams clear, actionable insight into the health and performance of mission-critical systems. This role sits within the DevSecOps organization and focuses on reliable, scalable telemetry collection, storage, visualization, and alerting across our environments.

This is a technical role for someone who enjoys making complex systems understandable and dependable. You will partner with Space Systems teams to improve monitoring coverage, alert quality, dashboard usability, and operational response. Your work will directly improve the reliability, performance, and security of software systems supporting space missions.

WHAT YOU'LL GET TO DO:

Build, operate, and continuously improve the organization's observability stack, including Grafana, Grafana Mimir, kube-prometheus-stack, and Grafana Alloy.
Design and maintain scalable metrics collection, ingestion, retention, and query patterns for Kubernetes and cloud-based workloads.
Develop and maintain Grafana dashboards that provide actionable insights to engineering teams and leadership.
Design, tune, and maintain alerting and notification workflows that reduce noise and enable timely, effective incident response.
Partner with engineering teams to define meaningful service-level indicators, service-level objectives, and monitoring standards.
Improve observability coverage by identifying telemetry gaps, analyzing trends, and implementing durable instrumentation and monitoring improvements.
Integrate AWS CloudWatch and CloudTrail telemetry into the observability platform to support operational visibility, security monitoring, and troubleshooting.
Manage observability infrastructure through version-controlled, automated deployments using Terraform, Git, and CI/CD pipelines.
Drive continuous improvement through data-driven analysis of platform reliability, telemetry quality, dashboard adoption, and alert effectiveness.
Troubleshoot complex monitoring, telemetry, and alerting issues across AWS, and GCP environments.
Work with development teams through code reviews and integrated pipelines to ensure observability is built in from the start.
Design and implement AI agents that detect, analyze, and troubleshoot software testing failures with minimal human intervention
Build and maintain AI-powered quality automation ecosystems that monitor CI/CD pipelines across multiple programs and platforms

YOU'LL BRING THESE QUALIFICATIONS:

Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, or other technical discipline
5+ years of experience in DevOps, site reliability engineering, platform engineering, or a related infrastructure discipline
Hands-on experience operating and improving production observability and monitoring platforms
Demonstrated expertise in AI/ML technologies with hands-on experience building AI-driven automation systems
Experience with AWS and GCP cloud services
Experience managing infrastructure as code with Terraform and collaborating through Git-based workflows
U.S. citizenship is required, due to program requirements

THESE QUALIFICATIONS WOULD BE NICE TO HAVE:

Experience with Splunk
Experience administering and configuring data visualization and analytics platforms, such as Grafana
Administration experience with Time Series Databases, such as Grafana Mimir
Strong problem-solving skills with an automation-first mindset and a track record of improving reliability in production environments
Experience deploying and managing Prometheus-based monitoring with kube-prometheus-stack
Experience configuring and operating Grafana Alloy for telemetry collection and forwarding
Strong understanding of CI/CD pipeline automation tools, DevSecOps practices, and Kubernetes operations
Experience with cloud networking concepts and troubleshooting
Experience building dashboards using tools like Grafana, Kibana, or custom visualization frameworks
Knowledge of security testing tools and DevSecOps security practices
Aerospace background supporting satellite, spacecraft, constellation, or launch vehicle ground/mission operations
Expertise in Git-based workflows, CI/CD pipelines, and Kubernetes orchestration
Experience with observability and monitoring tools
Experience with Kubecost
Operating and building solutions within GovCloud environment

This position may require prolonged periods of sitting, standing, walking, computer work, and occasional exposure to moderate levels of noise, dust, and fumes in production areas.

WHAT TO EXPECT

We're on a mission to unlock the potential of space to improve life on Earth, but that's not an easy task. It takes hard work, determination, relentless innovation, teamwork, grit, and an unwavering commitment to achieving what others often deem impossible. Our people out-think, out-work, and out-pace. We pride ourselves on having each other's backs, checking our egos at the door, and rolling up our sleeves on all tasks big and small. We thrive under pressure, work to tight deadlines, and our focus is always on how we can deliver, rather than dwelling on the challenges that stand in the way.

title: Machine Learning Engineer
description:
Company Description

Chooch helps build and run the best Computer Vision AI applications that make cameras intelligent, enhancing productivity & revenues, while reducing operational costs. Chooch has been named a leading computer vision platform by IDC.

Role Description

We are looking for a Machine Learning Engineer (US-based) to join our team. This is a full-time, hybrid role with frequent hands-on experience with customer projects in the Bay Area. The Machine Learning Engineer will be responsible for the successful design, accuracy, and backbone behind our Computer Vision AI applications. This includes data preparation, training, configuring neural networks, deploying networks in real customer locations, and refining computer vision algorithms for healthcare, manufacturing, and retail customers. This role requires frequent interaction with technical and non-technical customers while working closely within our solutions engineering teams. The Machine Learning Engineering role has opportunity to grow, lead technical projects, and improve current processes while providing meaningful feedback to our product and solutions teams.

Product Description Chooch AI is a computer vision platform that helps hospitals automate supply room monitoring and inventory management. Using fixed cameras and AI, the platform continuously tracks supplies in storage areas and updates on-hand counts in real time. When inventory levels fall below defined thresholds, replenishment orders are automatically generated and sent to ERP systems, eliminating manual counts and barcode scanning. Hospitals using Chooch AI significantly reduce critical stockouts, optimize inventory levels, and improve supply chain staff productivity. By turning supply rooms into self-managing systems, Chooch AI enables clinical and supply chain teams to focus more time on patient care.

Responsibilities/What you'll do at Chooch:

Design, train and fine-tune models for object detection, classification, segmentation, tracking and anomaly detection on real customer video and images.
Adapt pretrained and foundation models (YOLO-family detectors, ViTs, CLIP-style and vision-language models) to new customer use cases with limited labeled data.
Own data pipelines end to end: curation, labeling guidelines, augmentation, synthetic data, and dataset versioning.
Optimize models for production and edge hardware using quantization, pruning, distillation, ONNX export and TensorRT, hitting agreed latency and accuracy targets.
Build evaluation suites with clear metrics (mAP, precision/recall, false-alarm rates per camera-hour) and catch regressions before release.
Deploy and monitor models in production, diagnose drift and failure cases, and close the loop with retraining.
Work with product, solutions engineers and customers to turn vague requirements into measurable model specs.
Write clean, tested, reviewed code and contribute to shared ML tooling.

Nice to have

Experience with vision-language models (CLIP, LLaVA-style models) or open-vocabulary detection.
Multi-object tracking and video analytics (re-identification, action recognition, temporal models).
Few-shot learning, active learning, or synthetic data generation for low-data domains.
MLOps tooling: MLflow or Weights & Biases, Kubernetes, Triton Inference Server, CI/CD for models.
Domain experience in Healthcare, retail and supply chain, manufacturing inspection, workplace safety or video surveillance.

Key Components

Model Development and Optimization: Design, develop, and optimize machine learning models for computer vision applications.
Data Management: Collaborate with ML engineers to ensure the collection, processing, and maintenance of high-quality datasets necessary for model training and testing.
Algorithm Implementation: Implement state-of-the-art computer vision algorithms to improve system accuracy and performance in real-world scenarios.
Cross-Functional Collaboration: Work closely within the solutions engineering team to integrate machine learning models into the broader product and systems.
On-Site Travel and Field Testing: Many of our projects are live deployments with major fortune 500 customers – testing new, innovative ML technologies. Traveling on site is sometimes needed to see the environment, test in the real-world, and ensure the technology is operating as expected.
Performance Evaluation: Regularly evaluate the performance of computer vision models, using both qualitative and quantitative methods, and iterate to enhance accuracy and efficiency.
Research and Innovation: Understanding of the latest developments in machine learning and computer vision, applying innovative approaches and technologies to solve complex challenges.
Stakeholder Engagement: Collaborate with internal and external stakeholders to understand their needs and translate them into effective technical solutions.
Problem-Solving: Address and troubleshoot complex problems that arise during the development and deployment of computer vision systems.

The ideal candidate should be deeply passionate about machine learning and its real-world applications, particularly in improving and leveraging state-of-the-art neural networks to make an impact.

Requirements

3–5 years of industry experience building ML systems, with at least 2 years focused on computer vision.
BS or MS in Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, Math or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.
Strong Python and hands-on experience with PyTorch (or TensorFlow) for training and debugging deep learning models.
Shipped at least one computer vision model to production, and can explain the trade-offs made along the way.
Solid grasp of CNN and transformer architectures for detection, segmentation and classification.
Experience with OpenCV and image/video processing: decoding streams, preprocessing, augmentation.
Working knowledge of model optimization for inference (ONNX, TensorRT, quantization or similar).
Comfortable with Docker, Git, Linux and training on GPUs in a cloud environment (AWS/Azure).
Sound ML fundamentals: loss functions, overfitting, class imbalance, evaluation metrics and experiment design.
Clear written and verbal communication, including explaining model behavior to non-ML stakeholders.

Benefits

Chooch offers extensive benefits including health, dental, vision insurance, 401K with 3% match, extensive PTO, and life insurance policies included.

title: Sr. Computer Vision/ML Scientist
description:
Aicadium's Applied Research team is looking for a senior computer vision / ML scientist to tackle open-world visual understanding with limited labels across 2D recognition, multimodal inspection, and 3D/4D perception. You will bring anomaly detection, zero- and few-shot recognition, and semantic segmentation to applied systems used across multiple industries, building on 2D and 3D vision foundation models and vision-language models (VLMs). You will also help shape the team's research roadmap, with a focus on 3D/4D reconstruction, spatial perception, and world models. This is a hybrid role based in San Diego, where our U.S. headquarters is located. The ideal candidate has deep hands-on experience in modern computer vision, has taken models beyond the prototype stage, and can own problems end-to-end while supporting the development of junior scientists.

Responsibilities:

Own applied research on vision problems (anomaly detection, zero- and few-shot recognition, and semantic segmentation) end-to-end, from problem framing and baselines through validated models.
Adapt and extend 2D and 3D vision foundation models and VLMs to industrial domains through fine-tuning, harness optimization, and distillation.
Develop multimodal (vision-language) methods for industrial inspection tasks.
Conduct applied research in 3D/4D reconstruction, spatial perception, world models, and physics-based simulations, from proof-of-concept prototypes to reusable internal capabilities.
Design data and evaluation strategy for low-label, long-tail settings: annotation plans, active learning, and evaluation protocols that translate to stronger performance in the field.
Systematically analyze and improve deployed vision systems. Collaborate with engineering and product teams to bring new models to production, and maintain and improve model quality after launch.
Provide technical guidance to junior scientists and communicate methods, results, and trade-offs to technical and non-technical stakeholders.

Skills & Requirements:

PhD or Master's in Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, Robotics, Machine Learning, or a related field with 4+ years of hands-on computer vision / ML experience; doctoral research counts toward this requirement.
Expertise in at least two of the following: anomaly detection, zero- and few-shot (open-vocabulary) recognition, semantic segmentation, or multimodal (vision-language) learning.
Experience adapting vision foundation models (e.g., DINOv3, JEPA-family models
, SAM series) and VLMs (e.g., the Qwen-VL series) to new domains.
Hands-on experience in 3D/4D reconstruction and spatial perception, including modern 3D foundation models (e.g., VGGT, MASt3R, Depth Anything 3), grounded in multi-view geometry and camera models.
Ability to independently define research problems and turn recent research into working prototypes, with rigorous experimental practice: strong baselines, ablations, and sound evaluation on real-world data, including rare-event and heavily imbalanced problems.
Strong proficiency in Python and PyTorch, with a solid foundation in applied mathematics (linear algebra, geometry, probability, statistics, optimization).
Clear written and verbal communication skills, including presenting research to technical and non-technical audiences and stakeholders.

Nice to Have:

Publications at top-tier venues (CVPR, ICCV, ECCV, NeurIPS, ICLR) or notable open-source contributions in related areas.
Experience bringing computer vision models from prototype to production or customer-facing deployment.
Experience generating synthetic training data with generative models or simulation, particularly for defects, anomalies, and rare or data-deficient scenarios and classes.
Domain experience in industrial inspection, manufacturing, aerospace, food processing, medical imaging, or other fields with similar rare-defect or visual verification problems.
Experience with world models, such as V-JEPA 2, NVIDIA Cosmos, or spatially grounded VLMs.
Experience with VLAs and transformer-based action planners.

About Us:

Aicadium is a global technology company delivering AI-powered industrial computer vision products into the hands of enterprises. With offices in Singapore and San Diego, California, and an international team of data scientists, engineers, and business strategists, Aicadium is operationalizing AI within organizations where advanced machine learning innovations were previously out of reach.

Team

Join a growing team of data scientists, machine learning, and software engineers in an agile development environment. Work together with some of the best in the field to tackle challenging projects and operationalize the solutions you develop across a variety of industries and use cases.

Culture

We work in a casual and collaborative startup environment. Every member of the team plays a key role in shaping the solutions we develop and creating positive business value for the companies we work with. We are building a hub of the best talent in San Diego, CA, but we are open to working with people all over the U.S.

Benefits

Aicadium has a great benefits package to come with your salary. Benefits include PTO, health, vision, and dental insurance, life and AD&D, 401k with matching, and more!

title: Senior Test Engineer
description:
Company Description

Oteemo is an industry-leading technology consulting firm at the forefront of AI-driven, cloud native, enterprise DevSecOps transformation. We build intelligent, automated, secure systems for organizations tackling their toughest technical and business challenges and we're pushing the boundaries of what AI, generative AI, and agentic systems can do in production, not just in theory. Join us and you'll work alongside recognized experts on cutting-edge projects that blend cloud native architecture, extreme automation, and AI/ML at the core. We foster a dynamic, inclusive, and collaborative culture built on continuous learning, where your ideas shape real outcomes for our clients. If you're passionate about building what's next in AI and cloud technology and want to do it with a team that sets the standard rather than follows it, Oteemo is where you belong.

Job Description

We're looking for a Senior Test Engineer to prove that a regulated energy utility's new non-persistent Azure developer desktops meet their SLA and security controls. Every phase ends in an exit gate judged against agreed targets: boot under about 1 minute, IDE cold start under about 15 seconds, source control and Copilot reachable 99% or more, and zero TLS-interception failures. You'll turn those targets into automated, repeatable tests and build the mocks and synthetic data that keep production out of the sandbox.

Key Responsibilities:

SLA & Performance Validation: Turn the SLA into a measurable test plan with pass/fail thresholds and own phase-gate acceptance; baseline the on-premises VDI and score AVD and Horizon on the same harness; automate logon, boot, IDE cold start, and concurrent-workload tests with Login Enterprise or LoadGen.

Connectivity & Toolchain Validation: Run synthetic reachability checks for Git, Copilot, artifact repositories, and MCP endpoints through inspected egress; write NuGet, npm, pip, and Docker smoke tests that catch TLS or endpoint-agent breakage first.

Security & State Validation: Run negative tests proving production is unreachable, public endpoints are denied, App Control and EPM behave as designed, and every action reaches the SIEM; prove desktops rebuild clean while repos, caches, and tooling survive.

Test Data, Mocks & Containers: Build synthetic data generators, masked-subset tooling, and mock APIs (WireMock, Postman, Microcks) so no test touches production; test container and compose workflows end to end.

Infrastructure Gates & Reporting: Test IaC and policy with Terratest or Pester; define the gate AXIOM-built candidate images must pass before Security approves; publish SLA scorecards and hand over the regression suite and runbooks.

Qualifications

Bachelor's degree in a related field (or equivalent practical experience).

7+ years in test or quality engineering, including 3+ years testing infrastructure, platforms, or cloud environments.

Automation: Strong skills in at least two of PowerShell, Python, C# / .NET, or TypeScript, with tests in CI/CD (Azure DevOps or GitHub Actions).

Performance & Azure: Load testing with k6, JMeter, Locust, or VDI-specific tools; hands-on Azure VMs, networking, and monitoring (Azure Monitor, Log Analytics / KQL); Docker and docker compose.

API Testing & Test Data: Postman / Newman, REST, and mock servers; synthetic data generation and masking.

Writes test plans and evidence packages that a security or compliance reviewer accepts.

Additional Information

We Value:

Drive: Passion and energy to implement quality technical solutions. Self-motivation and intellectual curiosity
Commitment to Quality: Passion to conceive and produce world-class solutions that drive real-world value for the customer
Customer Focus: Consultative approach to solving problems for customers. Expectations management.
Communication: Superior communication skills. Ability to clearly articulate problems, solutions, risks, rewards etc. (written and verbal)
Technical Skills: Love for technology. You have to be inherently passionate about technology.
Business Acumen: Technology ultimately is used to enable the business. We look for people who understand how the businesses can be enabled through their technical solutions

All your information will be kept confidential according to EEO guidelines.

title: Lead AI Architect
description:
Company Description

Domino’s is a purpose-inspired, performance-driven company powered by exceptional people who are committed to feeding the power of possible—one pizza at a time. Founded in 1960 as a single store in Ypsilanti, Michigan, Domino’s has grown into the largest pizza company in the world, with more than 22,300 stores across 90+ markets. Our success is built on the strength of our people, technology, and franchise system. As a leader in innovation, we continue to transform the pizza and QSR industry while creating opportunities for team members to learn, grow and thrive. If you're ready to make an impact, build a meaningful career and help shape what's next, there's a place for you at Domino's.

Job Description

As Lead AI Architect, you own the technical architecture for Domino's enterprise AI platform – spanning classical AI, generative AI, and agentic AI. This is the senior individual-contributor technical authority on AI: you set the direction for how AI capabilities are built, served, orchestrated, and governed, and you drive outcomes through design authority and influence rather than direct reports. You own the reference architecture and the paved road teams build on, and the build-depth judgment for every incoming ask – production now, minimum viable, scaffolded as a contract for later, or deliberately deferred rather than quietly dropped.

This is a deeply hands-on role for an architect who has delivered AI platforms and solutions at enterprise scale – someone who knows why a technique works and when it survives contact with enterprise data, latency budgets, unit economics, and governance, and who still builds prototypes and reference implementations. Our environment is Azure-primary with Databricks.

Responsibilities

Architecture Ownership and Direction

Own the enterprise AI reference architecture end to end, establishing scalable standards, principles, and design patterns across business groups.
Own the roadmap for agentic systems platforms, translating business objectives into sequenced technical strategy, milestones, and a build-depth decision for every use case with explicit, traceable reasoning.
Design and maintain the paved road for AI development – golden patterns for building, serving, evaluating, and integrating models and agents, with an API-first integration default, MCP by exception against explicit criteria, and guardrails inherited rather than bolted on per team – so teams ship without re-solving solved problems.
Guide optimization of AI compute and token usage as adoption scales, and lead build-versus-buy, model, and framework decisions with evidence – benchmarks, cost per answer, real-load latency.

Semantic Search, Retrieval and RAG Architecture

Chunking, embedding and indexing: design chunking strategy per content type and tune size, overlap, and boundaries against measured retrieval quality; select and evaluate embedding models; own re-embedding and versioning.
Query construction and hybrid retrieval: implement query rewriting, decomposition, and expansion; combine dense and sparse retrieval with fusion and re-ranking; manage the recall-versus-precision and latency trade-off explicitly.
Retrieval and response evaluation: instrument recall, precision and faithfulness against curated golden datasets; ground answers in the certified semantic layer and knowledge graphs where they outperform vector retrieval; design for graceful abstention over confident wrong answers.

Generative AI Portfolio

Define prompt and instruction management standards – versioning, templating, context budgeting, and regression testing on prompt or model changes.
Own the AI gateway and multi-model routing, matching each request to the right model on complexity, cost, latency, and quality, and own the benchmarking discipline for how models are compared, selected, and re-tested as the landscape shifts.
Establish the evaluation harness as a launch gate – offline/online evaluation, LLM-as-judge with human calibration, A/B and shadow testing, and an explicit quality threshold we won't launch below.
Hold a clear, evidence-based position on when prompt engineering suffices versus when fine-tuning or customization is warranted, and define caching strategy as a deliberate cost and latency lever.

Agentic AI Portfolio

Architect the orchestration layer that chains agents, tools, retrieval, and human review – orchestration as the enforced contract, domain agents scoped by journey and business context, and a reusable skills and tool layer where reusability actually lives.
Design memory and context management with an explicit position on what persists, for how long, and under what access rules; define enterprise standards for tool/function calling and MCP server contracts.
Establish agent guardrails – authorization scope, permission models, approval and escalation paths, sandboxing, fallback behavior, and safe failure – plus step-level tracing, regression testing, audit, and incident response.
Define the agent registry, tool catalog, memory and state services, and lifecycle from prototype to monitored production asset, and apply agentic patterns – spec-driven development, AI-assisted code and test generation – to our own engineering practice.

Governance, Trust and Security

Define responsible AI standards – bias/fairness testing, transparency, explainability, and human oversight on high-risk outputs – aligned with enterprise data governance policy rather than parallel to it.
Establish AI security patterns for prompt injection, data exfiltration, jailbreaks, and model/supply-chain risk; partner with the Data Governance team on classification, stewardship, certified sources, and access controls – Microsoft Purview, Entra ID, Unity Catalog, row-level security, PII handling, and retention.
Classify use cases by risk, drive attestation with Security, Legal, Privacy, and Risk, and lead third-party model/vendor technical review, translating findings into architecture constraints.

Observability, Economics and Platform Engineering

Instrument tracing, telemetry, and drift signals from day one so agent behavior is observable before it's questioned; build cost attribution and drive cost per successful answer as a first-class metric.
Contribute to the instrumentation that ties AI investment to measurable outcomes –partnering with platform and finance teams so unit economics are a first-class design constraint.
Define the Azure-native platform stack and lifecycle with MLOps and Engineering – Azure AI Foundry, Azure ML, AKS, model/agent registry, CI/CD, landing-zone and environment strategy, Entra ID and network patterns, capacity, and LLMOps/AgentOps for versioning, promotion, and rollback.
Partner with Engineering and Architecture teams on data readiness, certified metrics, lineage, and data contracts, and with Engineering on turning reference patterns into shipped services – defining the sanctioned builder environment so teams move fast without bypassing controls.

Technical Leadership

Raise the bar across Engineering and solution architecture through design reviews, system-level reasoning, and mentorship – driving rigor without direct reporting relationships.
Translate architecture trade-offs into clear, decision-oriented narratives for senior technology leaders and peer architects, and lead cross-team decisions with partners such as Microsoft, Databricks, strategic AI vendors, and systems integrators.
Write architecture decision records, reference patterns, and reusable accelerators, and develop proof-of-concept reference implementations that help teams move AI solutions from concept through production without rebuilding the controls.

Qualifications

Deep enterprise architecture and systems-design expertise. Proven ability to design end-to-end AI platforms spanning applications, models, data, APIs, integration, identity, infrastructure, and operations. Strong grounding in distributed systems, event-driven and service-oriented patterns, resilience, high availability, fault tolerance, and disciplined architectural decision-making.
Strong foundations in AI, machine learning, and generative AI. Deep understanding of classical ML, deep learning, NLP, foundation models, transformers, embeddings, semantic retrieval, RAG, fine-tuning, multimodal AI, and agentic or multi-agent architectures, including when to use each approach, how to weigh the trade-offs, and where each one can fail.
Data, retrieval, and knowledge architecture expertise. Ability to design structured and unstructured data ingestion, transformation pipelines, chunking and indexing strategies, vector and hybrid retrieval, knowledge graphs, metadata models, lineage, provenance, data quality, and access controls, including grounding conversational experiences in structured data (text-to-SQL, multi-turn dialogue).
Model evaluation and production lifecycle engineering. Experience establishing evaluation frameworks and benchmarks (recall@k, NDCG, groundedness, LLM-as-judge), automated testing, release controls, model and prompt versioning, observability, quality monitoring, incident response, rollback, and ongoing improvement using MLOps and LLMOps principles.
Security, privacy, responsible AI, and governance. Ability to build identity, authorization, privacy, model security, human oversight, regulatory controls, and auditability into the architecture from the start. Must understand AI-specific threats such as prompt injection, sensitive-data leakage, unsafe agent actions, and model or software supply-chain risk.
Scalability, reliability, performance, and AI economics. Ability to make quantitative architecture decisions on latency, throughput, concurrency, availability, capacity, inference architecture, compute utilization, quality-versus-performance trade-offs, consumption forecasting, and cost optimization, including AI FinOps at scale.
Business and value-oriented solution architecture. Ability to translate business strategy into qualified AI use cases, measurable outcomes, target-state architectures, investment priorities, and delivery roadmaps. Must separate value-producing opportunities from technology demos and tie solutions to operational or financial KPIs.
End-to-end delivery with hands-on technical credibility. Demonstrated ability to move from discovery and architecture through experimentation, production deployment, and operational improvement. Able to build or review prototypes (Python, SQL, Spark), validate assumptions, review implementation designs, diagnose cross-layer failures, and defend technical trade-offs, with production depth in DevSecOps, Infrastructure as Code, Kubernetes, and model serving.
Technical leadership and stakeholder influence. Experience defining reusable patterns and standards, leading architecture reviews, mentoring engineers and architects, and aligning product, data science, engineering, infrastructure, security, and business teams. Creates clarity in ambiguity, leads with integrity and humility, and communicates well with executives and practitioners alike.
Substantial enterprise AI delivery experience. A strong record of leading complex AI or ML solutions in production at enterprise scale, typically 10+ years across software, data, or ML engineering with significant architecture leadership.

Preferred Qualifications

Hands-on experience with Microsoft environment: Azure (AI Foundry and Agent Service, Azure OpenAI, Azure ML, AI Search, API Management, Functions), Databricks and Copilot Studio; agent frameworks such as LangGraph or Semantic Kernel and MCP.
Experience in retail, restaurant, e-commerce, or supply chain with high-volume, real-time workloads and streaming (Kafka, Event Hubs) and model risk management.
Production multi-agent systems and agent runtimes, policy-aware agent gateways with authenticated tool routing and server registries, and GPU-accelerated serving stacks.
Contributions to open-source AI projects, published work, or recognized community involvement.

Additional Information

Benefits:

Paid Holidays and Vacation
Medical, Dental & Vision benefits that start on the first day of employment
No-cost mental health support for employee and dependents
Childcare tuition discounts
No-cost fitness, nutrition, and wellness programs
Fertility benefits
Adoption assistance
401k matching contributions
15% off the purchase price of stock
Company bonus

All your information will be kept confidential according to EEO guidelines.

title: GenAI Fullstack Engineer
description:
Marlabs, a global AI and Digital Solutions Consulting firm, delivers intelligent solutions across AI, data, analytics, and product engineering. Since 2000, we have partnered with some of the largest healthcare, life sciences, financial services, and government organizations worldwide. As we continue to expand our global footprint, we have an exciting opportunity for a highly skilled GenAI Fullstack Engineer to join our innovative and dynamic team.

This position requires onsite 5 days/week

GenAI Fullstack Engineer | About the Role

As a GenAI Fullstack Engineer, you will design and build scalable enterprise applications that combine robust Java-based backend engineering with modern Generative AI capabilities. You will work across Java, Spring Boot, Microservices, Python, FastAPI, LLMs, RAG, and Vector Databases to develop production-ready AI services and integrate them with enterprise applications. The ideal candidate is a strong software engineer who has expanded into hands-on GenAI engineering and can develop secure, scalable solutions spanning traditional backend services, AI orchestration, enterprise knowledge retrieval, and LLM-powered applications.

GenAI Fullstack Engineer | Day-to-Day

Design, develop, and maintain scalable backend applications and REST APIs using Java, Spring Boot, Microservices, Spring Security, and Spring Data/JPA.
Build and integrate production-grade GenAI and LLM applications, connecting AI services with existing Java/Spring Boot enterprise applications and business systems.
Design and implement Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) pipelines, including document ingestion, chunking, embeddings, indexing, semantic search, context retrieval, reranking, and response generation.
Develop AI services and orchestration components using Python and FastAPI, leveraging frameworks such as LangChain, LangGraph, LlamaIndex, or Hugging Face to support reusable enterprise AI capabilities.
Implement and optimize Vector Databases such as Pinecone, Weaviate, OpenSearch, FAISS, or ChromaDB to enable enterprise knowledge retrieval and semantic search.
Integrate LLM platforms such as Azure OpenAI, OpenAI, AWS Bedrock, Claude, Gemini, or Llama, applying prompt engineering, response evaluation, guardrails, and optimization techniques to improve solution accuracy and reliability.
Build secure and observable AI/backend services by implementing authentication, authorization, exception handling, logging, monitoring, API security, and production-grade engineering standards.
Containerize and deploy applications using Docker and CI/CD pipelines, collaborating with architects, data engineers, developers, and business teams to deliver reliable and scalable GenAI solutions.

GenAI Fullstack Engineer | Skills & Experience

Strong software engineering 3+ years experience with Java, Spring Boot, Microservices, and REST APIs, including hands-on experience designing scalable and distributed enterprise backend applications.
Hands-on experience developing production GenAI/LLM applications, including LLM integration, prompt engineering, response evaluation, and enterprise AI use cases.
Strong production experience with RAG architectures, including embeddings, document ingestion, chunking, semantic retrieval, reranking, context construction, and RAG quality optimization.
Strong working knowledge of Python and FastAPI, with experience building AI/ML services and integrating Python-based AI components with Java/Spring Boot applications.
Hands-on experience with Vector Databases and GenAI frameworks, such as Pinecone, Weaviate, OpenSearch, FAISS, ChromaDB, LangChain, LangGraph, LlamaIndex, or Hugging Face.
Experience with cloud and modern deployment practices, including AWS, Azure, or GCP, Docker, CI/CD, monitoring, observability, and production deployment of AI services.
Additional exposure to Agentic AI, MCP (Model Context Protocol), AI guardrails, LLMOps, Kubernetes, knowledge graphs, multimodal AI, and event-driven microservices is advantageous.

title: Data Engineer
description:

title: Forward Deployed Engineer, AI
description:
Arrowhead Pharmaceuticals, Inc. (Nasdaq ARWR) is a commercial stage biopharmaceutical company that develops medicines that treat intractable diseases by silencing the genes that cause them. Using a broad portfolio of RNA chemistries and efficient modes of delivery, Arrowhead therapies trigger the RNA interference mechanism to induce rapid, deep, and durable knockdown of target genes. RNA interference, or RNAi, is a mechanism present in living cells that inhibits the expression of a specific gene, thereby affecting the production of a specific protein. Arrowhead's RNAi-based therapeutics leverage this natural pathway of gene silencing.

Arrowhead is focused on developing innovative drugs for diseases with a genetic basis, typically characterized by the overproduction of one or more proteins that are involved with disease. The depth and versatility of our RNAi technologies enables us to potentially address conditions in virtually any therapeutic area and pursue disease targets that are not otherwise addressable by small molecules and biologics. Arrowhead is leading the field in bringing the promise of RNAi to address diseases outside of the liver, and our clinical pipeline includes disease targets in the liver and lung with a promising pipeline of preclinical candidates.

Arrowhead's corporate headquarters is in Pasadena, CA with research and development teams in Madison, WI & San Diego, CA, and a state of the art manufacturing facility in Verona, WI. Our employees are nimble, science-driven innovators who are collaborating to bring new therapies to patients in need.

The Position

This is a newly created, green-field role and the first Forward Deployed Engineer, AI hired within the company. The person in this role will partner directly with business and scientific stakeholders across multiple functions to identify high-value problems and build and deploy AI-driven solutions that solve them. Because there is no existing playbook for this function, the Forward Deployed Engineer will help define how AI solutions are scoped, built, and delivered internally, working hands-on across the AWS, Azure, Databricks, and Microsoft technology stack alongside the Data Platform Engineer, DevOps Engineer, and Databricks/AWS platform teams. This role requires someone comfortable operating with ambiguity, moving quickly from problem discovery to a working solution, and embedding directly with internal teams to understand their workflows before proposing and shipping AI tools that fit how they actually work.

Responsibilities

Partner directly with stakeholders across R&D, clinical, manufacturing, commercial, and other business functions to identify, scope, and prioritize opportunities for AI-driven internal solutions.
Design, build, and deploy agentic AI workflows and applications that solve real operational and scientific problems, working end-to-end from prototype through production.
Establish foundational engineering practices, standards, and reusable patterns for AI solution delivery, since this is the first role of its kind in the organization.
Work closely with the Data Platform Engineer to access, model, and productionize data needed for AI solutions across Databricks and AWS.
Collaborate with the DevOps Engineer to build reliable CI/CD pipelines, deployment processes, and monitoring for AI applications across AWS/ Databricks inside a MS environments.
Leverage the Databricks platform and AWS services (e.g., Bedrock, Lambda, S3) to build and orchestrate agentic AI workflows and applications, primarily by composing and integrating existing foundation models rather than training new ones.
Integrate solutions with Microsoft/Azure tools (e.g., Azure AI services, M365) where appropriate to meet business needs.
Rapidly prototype proof-of-concepts with internal teams, gather feedback, and iterate quickly to move validated solutions into production.
Document architecture, decisions, and delivery patterns to build a repeatable internal playbook for future forward-deployed engineering work.
Act as a hands-on technical resource embedded with business teams, translating ambiguous business problems into concrete technical solutions.

Requirements

Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Engineering, Data Science, or a related technical field, or equivalent practical experience.
5+ years of professional software engineering experience, including building and deploying production-grade applications.
Hands-on experience with AWS cloud services and Azure/Microsoft cloud services.
Experience working with Databricks, including data engineering, notebooks, and/or ML workflows.
Strong proficiency in at least one modern programming language (e.g., Python, SQL, or similar) used for building data and AI applications.
Demonstrated experience building agentic workflows and applications with generative AI and LLM-based approaches (e.g., orchestration frameworks, tool use, retrieval-augmented generation) to solve practical business problems.
Proven ability to work independently in ambiguous, undefined environments and to build solutions from the ground up without an established playbook.
Strong cross-functional communication skills, with the ability to translate technical concepts for non-technical business stakeholders and vice versa.

Preferred

Knowledge of the pharmaceutical, biotech, or life sciences industry is desirable but not required.
Experience with Databricks certifications, AWS certifications, or Microsoft Azure certifications.
Prior experience in a "forward deployed engineer," solutions engineering, or embedded engineering role, working directly with business teams rather than in a purely centralized product function.
Experience with LLMOps/agent-ops tooling and practices for deploying, monitoring, and evaluating agentic workflows in production.
Familiarity with regulated-industry considerations (e.g., data privacy, validation, GxP) relevant to deploying AI solutions in a pharma environment.
Experience building internal tools, chatbots, or agentic AI applications using modern LLM frameworks.
A builder mindset with the initiative to define scope and process in a green-field function.

Arrowhead provides competitive salaries and an excellent benefit package.

Candidates must have current, valid authorization to work in the country where this role is located.

title: Data Scientist
description:
Data Scientist

On-site in Longmont, Colorado. Monday through Friday, business hours, Mountain Time.

About Docketly

Docketly, a sister company to ABC Legal Services, is a fast-growing legal-tech company based in Longmont, Colorado. For the creditors' rights industry, we make hiring a stand-in attorney easy, fast, and reliable. We pair proprietary software with a nationwide network of attorneys.

Job Overview

You build and run the machine learning and analytics systems behind Docketly's operations. You build and run production models, from first idea to a live, monitored system on AWS. ABC Legal's data science team is your sounding board on methods. You build the BI reporting that leadership, operations, and client teams use daily. You support pricing and margin decisions with financial modeling. You work closely with backend engineers on data infrastructure and production issues. This role can grow into Senior Data Scientist as you take full ownership of the production model and the pricing roadmap.

Key Responsibilities

Model development and MLOps

Build and run the full lifecycle of production ML models: framing, feature engineering, training, validation, deployment on AWS SageMaker (Model Registry, real-time endpoints), inference infrastructure (for example, AWS Lambda), and ongoing monitoring.
Build and maintain automated retraining and drift monitoring for deployed models.
Run staged production rollouts with holdout comparisons to prove model impact before full release. Review the test design with the team before launch.
Use AI coding tools to speed up analysis, modeling, and MLOps work.

Analytics, pricing, and reporting

Build and maintain the BI layer leadership relies on for exec reporting on revenue, margin, and volume, from dashboard design through data accuracy.
Run pricing and margin analysis for client accounts, including ad hoc investigations for named strategic accounts. Model the financial impact of proposed pricing changes before they go live.
Build and maintain rules-based pricing and case-difficulty logic by court and county, alongside statistical and ML approaches.
Build and tune large scoring and prioritization frameworks in Metabase, such as weighting, percentile scenarios, and drop-rate analysis, that drive daily operational decisions such as Hearing priority and assignment.
Turn ambiguous business questions into clear, well-scoped analyses.

Cross-functional partnership and documentation

Partner with engineering on data pipelines (AWS Glue, Lambda, EventBridge). Investigate and help resolve production database performance issues, such as ORM query patterns and indexing, alongside backend engineering.
Write down your methods and decisions in Confluence or an equivalent shared space, as you go, so other teams can find your reasoning and build on it without asking you directly.

Systems & Skills

Required

Bachelor's degree in a related field, or equivalent practical experience, and 3+ years of experience with applied statistics or machine learning.
Applied statistics: probability, hypothesis testing, and model evaluation across classification and regression/quantile models (for example, precision, recall, calibration, quantile coverage, and drift).
3+ years of experience with SQL and a relational database in a professional capacity. Docketly's production database runs on MySQL/Aurora, about 400 tables.
Python for data analysis and modeling: pandas, scikit-learn, and a gradient-boosting framework (XGBoost, LightGBM, or CatBoost). Our production model uses CatBoost-based quantile regression.
Experience training and deploying at least one model to production, or on a cloud ML platform such as AWS SageMaker.
Metabase or comparable BI tooling.
Clear written and verbal communication with non-technical stakeholders.

Preferred

Staged production rollouts (canary or phased release) with holdout comparisons to prove model impact before full release.
AWS Glue, S3, Lambda, EventBridge, CloudFormation.
Comfortable using AI coding tools such as Claude Code or GitHub Copilot to move faster on analysis and modeling work.
Experience diagnosing production database performance issues, such as query plans, indexing, and ORM-generated query patterns, in a large, high-table-count schema.
Software-engineering practices applied to ML code, such as automated testing with pytest, for production pipelines.

Benefits

Health, Dental, and Vision Insurance
401(k) with Company Matching
Paid Time Off
7 Paid Company Holidays
4 Floating Holidays per Year
Life Insurance and AD&D Insurance
Long-Term Disability
Health Care Reimbursement Flexible Spending Account (FSA)
Dependent Care Flexible Spending Account
Employee Assistance Program (EAP)
Pet Insurance

Schedule: Monday-Friday, 8:00 AM-5:00 PM (Mountain Time) in Longmont, CO.

Salary Range: $110,000-$130,000 depending on experience

title: Staff Platform Engineer
description:
Description:

The Staff Platform Engineer sets the technical direction for the platform and solves infrastructure problems that span teams. The role stays hands-on — writing and reviewing infrastructure code and operating production systems — but most of its impact comes from shaping how the whole engineering organization builds, deploys, and runs software, without formal management authority. Staff engineers may also serve as a team's Tech Lead, a role that carries no change in title, band, or bonus.

Regularly audit and evaluate the platform's architecture, and lead the design and delivery of major
architectural changes across teams on an annual basis.
Write technical proposals for those changes and build agreement on them with product and engineering
stakeholders.
Set org-wide standards for infrastructure patterns, delivery practices, tooling, and technology choices.
Partner with Buyer and Cargo engineering leadership so the platform supports what their teams need to build
next.
Define observability, reliability, and incident standards, and take on the hardest production problems: systemic
bottlenecks, performance crises, and failures under heavy contention.
Plan and carry out large migrations, such as database moves, network re-architecture, and project
restructuring, without disrupting live auctions.
Own the platform's security, cost, and capacity strategy.
Mentor senior engineers and act as a force multiplier, influencing direction without formal authority.

CockroachDB, PgBouncer, or large-scale database migration and replication.
Cloud Armor, WAF, or bot-mitigation experience.
Vertex AI or other ML serving infrastructure.
Experience architecting systems with heavy write contention, such as many users acting on the same records at once in bidding, inventory, or payments.
