title: Senior Scientist I, Cheminformatics
description:
Eikon Therapeutics is a new biopharmaceutical company employing revolutionary technology at the intersection of chemistry, engineering, computation, and biology to discover novel treatments for life-threatening diseases. Eikon's discovery platform is built on groundbreaking innovations from its founders (Nobel Prize, 2014), culminating in the creation of microscopes which enable real time, molecular-resolution measurements of protein movement in living cells, thereby unlocking otherwise intractable classes of proteins as drug targets.

Position

We seek a Senior Scientist with a demonstrated ability of successfully applying Cheminformatics and ML technologies to drive the discovery programs. You will collaborate closely with computational chemists, medicinal chemists, software engineers and machine learning experts to turn assay and structure-activity data into interpretable information for decision making. As an integral member of our Drug Discovery team, you will make a real and direct impact on accelerating the drug discovery process and ultimately benefiting patients.

About You

You're a cheminformatics expert who loves to solve difficult problems and are not discouraged by challenges. You have a passion for drug discovery and thrive in a fast-paced, dynamic environment. You are curious, love challenges, and enjoy pushing the edge of technology to solve important problems with creative solutions. You're collaborative by nature, resourceful, open-minded, data-driven, and can operate with a sense of urgency.

What You'll Do

Develop and apply cheminformatics data-mining algorithms for the analysis of molecular modeling, virtual screening, and structure-activity relationship (SAR) analysis.
Process and analyze chemical and biological datasets to evaluate properties such as drug-likeness, ADMET properties, dosing, etc.
Utilize molecular fingerprints, descriptors, and similarity metrics for compound clustering, classification, and regression.
Assist in development, maintenance, and monitoring of AI/ML models used for property prediction.
Optimize data pipelines for processing and storing chemical structures using cheminformatics toolkits (e.g., RDKit).
Collaborate with cross-functional teams to integrate computational approaches into curation and analysis workflows.
Maintain best practices in data integrity, reproducibility, and documentation of QSAR AI/ML models.
Provide guidance on the application of modern cheminformatics, ML/AI methods for library design (e.g. diversity, focused, fragment, DEL) and analyzing large datasets from HTS campaigns to building predictive models from them.
Routinely employ expert knowledge and analysis of SAR, physiochemical and ADMET properties.
Work alongside medicinal chemists to further triage emerging hits from HTS.
Collaborate closely with our data science team to integrate cutting edge AI/ML tools into our chemistry and drug discovery processes.

Qualifications

Ph.D. plus 5 years of relevant experience; or Master's plus 14 years of relevant experience; or Bachelor's plus 16 years of relevant experience.
Expertise in cheminformatics data analysis, data mining, and machine learning models to solve drug discovery problems.
Expertise with ligand-based design approaches, QSAR, multiparameter optimization to rationalize SAR and design novel molecules.
Expertise in scientific programming languages such as python, with experience using RDKit and other cheminformatic libraries and data analytics (Spotfire, DataWarrior, D360).
Experience in virtual screening, HTS triaging, hit calling, and diversity analysis.
Familiar with commercial platforms and ELN/registration systems (Schrödinger, OpenEye, MOE, Dotmatics, DataBricks, KNIME).
A track record of publications, patents and/or conference presentations in computational chemistry and/or drug discovery.
Excellent problem-solving abilities and the ability to work in a fast-paced, dynamic research environment.
Strong communication skills with the ability to convey complex scientific concepts to both technical and non-technical stakeholders.

At Eikon, employee compensation also includes bonus and equity compensation, in addition to several generous benefit programs, including:

401k plan with company matching
Medical (premiums covered by Eikon at 95%), dental and vision insurance (premiums covered by Eikon at 100%)
Mental health and wellness benefits
Weeklong summer and winter holiday shutdowns
Generous paid time off and holiday policies
Life/AD&D Insurance (premiums covered by Eikon at 100%) and optional supplemental employee-paid life/AD&D policies
Enhanced parental leave benefit
Daily subsidized lunch program when on-site

The expected salary range for this role is $178,000 to $215,250 depending on skills, competency, and the market demand for your expertise.

Eikon is proud to be an equal opportunity employer and will consider all qualified applicants for employment.

We are currently not accepting any new third-party agencies or firms at this time. Please do not forward unsolicited agency resumes to our website, employees or Human Resources. Eikon Therapeutics will not pay fees to any third-party agency or firm associated with unsolicited resumes.

description:

title: Machine Learning Engineer
description:

title: Sr. Computer Vision/ML Scientist
description:
Aicadium's Applied Research team is looking for a senior computer vision / ML scientist to tackle open-world visual understanding with limited labels across 2D recognition, multimodal inspection, and 3D/4D perception. You will bring anomaly detection, zero- and few-shot recognition, and semantic segmentation to applied systems used across multiple industries, building on 2D and 3D vision foundation models and vision-language models (VLMs). You will also help shape the team's research roadmap, with a focus on 3D/4D reconstruction, spatial perception, and world models. This is a hybrid role based in San Diego, where our U.S. headquarters is located. The ideal candidate has deep hands-on experience in modern computer vision, has taken models beyond the prototype stage, and can own problems end-to-end while supporting the development of junior scientists.

Responsibilities:

Own applied research on vision problems (anomaly detection, zero- and few-shot recognition, and semantic segmentation) end-to-end, from problem framing and baselines through validated models.
Adapt and extend 2D and 3D vision foundation models and VLMs to industrial domains through fine-tuning, harness optimization, and distillation.
Develop multimodal (vision-language) methods for industrial inspection tasks.
Conduct applied research in 3D/4D reconstruction, spatial perception, world models, and physics-based simulations, from proof-of-concept prototypes to reusable internal capabilities.
Design data and evaluation strategy for low-label, long-tail settings: annotation plans, active learning, and evaluation protocols that translate to stronger performance in the field.
Systematically analyze and improve deployed vision systems. Collaborate with engineering and product teams to bring new models to production, and maintain and improve model quality after launch.
Provide technical guidance to junior scientists and communicate methods, results, and trade-offs to technical and non-technical stakeholders.

Skills & Requirements:

PhD or Master's in Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, Robotics, Machine Learning, or a related field with 4+ years of hands-on computer vision / ML experience; doctoral research counts toward this requirement.
Expertise in at least two of the following: anomaly detection, zero- and few-shot (open-vocabulary) recognition, semantic segmentation, or multimodal (vision-language) learning.
Experience adapting vision foundation models (e.g., DINOv3, JEPA-family models
, SAM series) and VLMs (e.g., the Qwen-VL series) to new domains.
Hands-on experience in 3D/4D reconstruction and spatial perception, including modern 3D foundation models (e.g., VGGT, MASt3R, Depth Anything 3), grounded in multi-view geometry and camera models.
Ability to independently define research problems and turn recent research into working prototypes, with rigorous experimental practice: strong baselines, ablations, and sound evaluation on real-world data, including rare-event and heavily imbalanced problems.
Strong proficiency in Python and PyTorch, with a solid foundation in applied mathematics (linear algebra, geometry, probability, statistics, optimization).
Clear written and verbal communication skills, including presenting research to technical and non-technical audiences and stakeholders.

Nice to Have:

Publications at top-tier venues (CVPR, ICCV, ECCV, NeurIPS, ICLR) or notable open-source contributions in related areas.
Experience bringing computer vision models from prototype to production or customer-facing deployment.
Experience generating synthetic training data with generative models or simulation, particularly for defects, anomalies, and rare or data-deficient scenarios and classes.
Domain experience in industrial inspection, manufacturing, aerospace, food processing, medical imaging, or other fields with similar rare-defect or visual verification problems.
Experience with world models, such as V-JEPA 2, NVIDIA Cosmos, or spatially grounded VLMs.
Experience with VLAs and transformer-based action planners.

About Us:

Aicadium is a global technology company delivering AI-powered industrial computer vision products into the hands of enterprises. With offices in Singapore and San Diego, California, and an international team of data scientists, engineers, and business strategists, Aicadium is operationalizing AI within organizations where advanced machine learning innovations were previously out of reach.

Join a growing team of data scientists, machine learning, and software engineers in an agile development environment. Work together with some of the best in the field to tackle challenging projects and operationalize the solutions you develop across a variety of industries and use cases.

We work in a casual and collaborative startup environment. Every member of the team plays a key role in shaping the solutions we develop and creating positive business value for the companies we work with. We are building a hub of the best talent in San Diego, CA, but we are open to working with people all over the U.S.

title: Senior Edge Algorithm Integration Engineer
description:
At WHOOP, we're on a mission to unlock and inspire performance for life. WHOOP empowers members to perform at a higher level through a deeper understanding of their bodies and daily lives.

WHOOP is hiring an Edge Algorithm Integration Engineer to join the Edge ML team and bring Sensor Intelligence algorithms from validated reference implementations to production execution on WHOOP devices. You will own the technical path from reference algorithm to edge deployment, translating and optimizing algorithms for embedded hardware, resolving cross-platform dependencies, integrating with firmware and sensor infrastructure, and ensuring implementations preserve expected algorithm performance. You will work across Sensor Intelligence, Firmware, Edge ML Platform, Mobile, Cloud, and Connectivity teams to enable algorithms to run reliably and efficiently within the compute, memory, latency, and power constraints of WHOOP devices.

RESPONSIBILITIES:

Own the end-to-end technical path for porting developed and validated Sensor Intelligence algorithms from reference environments to production-ready implementations on WHOOP embedded platforms.

Translate Python, MATLAB, and other reference implementations into efficient, production-quality C/C++, optimizing signal-processing and machine-learning algorithms for compute, memory, latency, power, and real-time execution.

Understand algorithm architecture, data flow, runtime requirements, and dependencies across cloud, mobile, connectivity, sensor pipelines, libraries, and platform services; drive the technical work required to resolve or redesign dependencies for on-device execution.

Integrate algorithms with firmware, sensor pipelines, embedded services, and Edge ML platform capabilities, partnering closely with Sensor Intelligence and Firmware teams to define interfaces, requirements, acceptance criteria, and system-level behavior.

Establish functional and numerical equivalence between reference and edge implementations, profile on-device performance, and debug complex issues spanning algorithms, sensors, firmware, and embedded systems.

Build reusable tools, test harnesses, profiling infrastructure, and deployment patterns that accelerate future algorithm migrations and enable efficient portability across current and next-generation WHOOP hardware platforms.

QUALIFICATIONS:

BS/MS in Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Computer Science, or a related technical field, or equivalent practical experience.

Strong C/C++ software development experience with embedded, real-time, or resource-constrained systems, including an understanding of memory management, compute limitations, latency, and power constraints.

Experience porting, integrating, or optimizing signal-processing or machine-learning algorithms for MCU-based, embedded, or edge platforms, including translating implementations from Python, MATLAB, or similar reference environments.

Experience profiling and optimizing embedded software for runtime, memory footprint, computational efficiency, and/or power, with strong debugging skills across algorithm and systems boundaries.

Strong systems thinking and software integration skills, with the ability to understand complex dependencies and collaborate across algorithm, firmware, platform, and other engineering teams to drive technical issues to resolution.

Experience with one or more relevant embedded optimization technologies or techniques, such as DSP optimization, fixed-point implementation, quantization, model compression, ARM Cortex-M, DSPs, NPUs, RTOS environments, CMSIS-DSP/CMSIS-NN, or TensorFlow Lite Micro.

Experience with physiological sensing, wearable devices, time-series sensor data, low-power systems, or establishing functional and numerical equivalence between reference and embedded implementations is a plus.

Strong commitment to embracing and leveraging AI tools in day-to-day tasks, ensuring AI-assisted work aligns with the same high-quality standards as personal contributions.

Interested in the role, but don’t meet every qualification? We encourage you to still apply! At WHOOP, we believe there is much more to a candidate than what is written on paper, and we value character as much as experience. As we continue to build a diverse and inclusive environment, we encourage anyone who is interested in this role to apply.

title: Java Architect
description:
Overview:

REI Systems’ mission is to deliver reliable, innovative technology solutions that advance Federal clients' missions and exceed their expectations. Our technologists and consultants are passionate about solving complex challenges that impact millions of lives. We take a Mindful Modernization® approach in delivering our services, including application modernization, grants management, case management systems, government data analytics, and advisory services. This approach, the REI Way, ensures mission impact by aligning our clients' strategic objectives with measurable outcomes through people, processes, and technology.

We offer the same commitment to our employees by providing professional development, meaningful projects, and flexibility to spend time with family and friends. We believe employees are at their best when fulfilled in both their professional careers and their personal lives. Learn more at www.REIsystems.com.

Employees voted REI Systems a Washington Post Top Workplace in 2015, 2016, 2018, 2020, 2021, 2022, 2023, 2024, and 2025!

Responsibilities:

Position Overview

REI Systems is seeking an experienced Java Architect to provide technical architecture, solution design, and hands-on engineering leadership for mission-critical applications supporting the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA).

The ideal candidate will bring deep expertise in Java, Spring Boot, microservices, RESTful APIs, AWS cloud services, and modern application architecture. This individual will be responsible for designing secure, scalable, resilient, and high-performing enterprise applications while guiding development teams through modernization initiatives, cloud adoption, system integration, and continuous delivery.

This position requires a strong technical leader who can balance enterprise architecture strategy with hands-on development, collaborate with FDA stakeholders, and ensure solutions meet federal security, compliance, performance, and operational requirements.

Key Responsibilities

Solution Architecture & Technical Leadership

Lead the architecture, design, and development of enterprise Java applications supporting FDA mission-critical systems.
Define application architecture, technical standards, integration patterns, and development best practices.
Design scalable, modular, maintainable solutions using Java, Spring Boot, Spring Framework, and microservices architecture.
Provide hands-on technical leadership through architecture reviews, design sessions, code reviews, and proof-of-concept development.
Translate business and functional requirements into technical architecture, solution designs, and implementation roadmaps.
Develop architecture diagrams, technical design documents, API specifications, and system integration documentation.
Evaluate legacy systems and recommend modernization strategies, including application refactoring, cloud migration, and API enablement.
Identify and resolve complex architectural challenges involving performance, scalability, availability, security, and interoperability.
Mentor Java developers and technical leads, promoting engineering excellence and consistent development practices.

Java Development & Microservices

Architect and develop enterprise applications using Java 11/17/21, Spring Boot, Spring MVC, Spring Security, and Spring Data JPA.
Design and implement RESTful APIs and microservices for distributed enterprise applications.
Apply design patterns, object-oriented programming principles, SOLID principles, and clean architecture practices.
Implement service-to-service communication, asynchronous processing, exception handling, and transaction management.
Design secure API integrations using OAuth 2.0, OpenID Connect, JWT, and API gateway patterns.
Work with Hibernate/JPA, JDBC, and ORM frameworks for database-driven applications.
Support event-driven architecture and messaging integrations using technologies such as Apache Kafka, RabbitMQ, or AWS messaging services, where applicable.
Establish automated unit, integration, and API testing standards using JUnit, Mockito, and related frameworks.

AWS Cloud Architecture & Modernization

Design, deploy, and optimize cloud-native and cloud-enabled applications within AWS environments.
Provide architectural guidance for AWS services such as EC2, ECS, EKS, Lambda, S3, RDS, API Gateway, IAM, CloudWatch, and CloudFormation.
Architect containerized applications using Docker and Kubernetes.
Support application modernization, cloud migration, and infrastructure automation initiatives.
Design highly available, fault-tolerant, secure, and cost-effective cloud solutions.
Collaborate with cloud infrastructure and DevOps engineers on deployment strategies, monitoring, scaling, and disaster recovery.
Apply AWS security, networking, identity management, and cloud architecture best practices.

Database Architecture & Integration

Design and optimize database integrations involving Oracle, PostgreSQL, SQL Server, and other relational databases.
Develop and review complex SQL queries, stored procedures, and PL/SQL components as applicable.
Provide guidance on database performance optimization, indexing, connection pooling, and data access patterns.
Design data integration solutions between enterprise applications, legacy platforms, and external systems.
Support data integrity, transaction management, and secure data exchange across distributed applications.

DevSecOps, CI/CD & Application Security

Collaborate with DevSecOps teams to establish automated build, testing, deployment, and release processes.
Support CI/CD pipelines using Jenkins, GitHub Actions, GitLab CI, or comparable enterprise tools.
Apply infrastructure-as-code practices using Terraform, AWS CloudFormation, or similar technologies.
Integrate automated code quality, dependency scanning, vulnerability detection, and security testing into development workflows.
Promote secure coding standards and address vulnerabilities identified through SAST, DAST, and software composition analysis.
Implement appropriate logging, monitoring, audit trails, and application observability.
Ensure architecture and development practices align with applicable federal security requirements, including NIST guidelines, FISMA, FedRAMP, and FDA-specific standards.

Agile Delivery & Stakeholder Collaboration

Collaborate with FDA technical stakeholders, product owners, business analysts, project managers, and development teams.
Participate in Agile ceremonies, including sprint planning, backlog refinement, architecture discussions, and release planning.
Work closely with QA engineers, database administrators, cloud engineers, and DevSecOps teams to ensure successful solution delivery.
Provide technical estimates, identify architectural risks, and recommend mitigation strategies.
Support technical troubleshooting, root-cause analysis, production issue resolution, and continuous application improvement.
Communicate complex technical concepts clearly to both technical and nontechnical stakeholders.
Qualifications:
10+ years of software engineering experience, with significant hands-on Java application development experience.
5+ years of experience in technical architecture, solution design, or technical leadership for enterprise applications.
Strong hands-on expertise in Java, Spring Boot, Spring Framework, Spring Security, and RESTful web services.
Demonstrated experience designing and implementing microservices and distributed enterprise applications.
Strong knowledge of object-oriented design, software design patterns, SOLID principles, and enterprise application architecture.
Experience designing, developing, or modernizing applications hosted on AWS.
Hands-on experience with Docker, Kubernetes, and containerized application deployments.
Experience with relational databases, particularly Oracle and PostgreSQL, including SQL optimization and data integration.
Experience with CI/CD pipelines, Git-based version control, Maven or Gradle, and automated development workflows.
Knowledge of API security, authentication, authorization, and secure software development practices.
Experience troubleshooting complex application issues, performance bottlenecks, and integration challenges.
Demonstrated ability to lead technical discussions, review architectural designs, and mentor software engineers.
Experience working in Agile/Scrum development environments.
Strong written and verbal communication skills, including experience interacting with technical leadership and business stakeholders.
Ability to obtain and maintain the background investigation or Public Trust clearance required for the FDA program.

Preferred Qualifications

Prior experience supporting FDA, HHS, or other federal civilian government IT programs.
Experience modernizing legacy Java applications and migrating enterprise workloads to AWS.
AWS Certified Solutions Architect – Associate or Professional certification.
Oracle, PostgreSQL, and PL/SQL development experience.
Experience with Apache Kafka, RabbitMQ, or event-driven architecture.
Familiarity with Angular, React, TypeScript, or other modern frontend frameworks.
Experience with enterprise API management, API Gateway, and integration platforms.
Experience with Terraform, Ansible, Kubernetes, and GitOps-based deployment approaches.
Familiarity with SonarQube, Fortify, Checkmarx, or comparable security and code quality tools.
Experience with application monitoring and observability using CloudWatch, Splunk, ELK, Prometheus, or Grafana.
Knowledge of Section 508 accessibility requirements and federal application security standards.
Experience with system modernization, cloud-native transformation, and enterprise integration initiatives.
Exposure to AI-enabled applications, AI/ML service integration, or intelligent workflow automation is a plus.

Technical Environment

Programming Languages: Java 11/17/21, SQL, PL/SQL, JavaScript, TypeScript

Backend Frameworks: Spring Boot, Spring MVC, Spring Security, Spring Data JPA, Hibernate, RESTful APIs

Cloud Technologies: AWS EC2, ECS, EKS, Lambda, S3, RDS, API Gateway, IAM, CloudWatch

Architecture: Microservices, SOA, Distributed Systems, REST APIs, Event-Driven Architecture, Cloud-Native Applications

Databases: Oracle, PostgreSQL, Microsoft SQL Server

DevSecOps & CI/CD: Git, Jenkins, GitHub Actions, Maven, Gradle, Docker, Kubernetes, Terraform, Ansible

Testing & Quality: JUnit, Mockito, Postman, Swagger/OpenAPI, SonarQube

Security: OAuth 2.0, OpenID Connect, JWT, NIST, FISMA, FedRAMP, OWASP

Methodologies: Agile, Scrum, DevSecOps, Secure SDLC

The technologies listed represent the relevant architecture and engineering ecosystem. Specific tools and versions may vary by FDA project and application.

What Success Looks Like

The successful Java Architect will:

Deliver secure, scalable, and maintainable Java-based enterprise solutions.
Establish consistent architecture and engineering standards across development teams.
Accelerate application modernization and cloud adoption while reducing technical debt.
Improve application reliability, performance, security, and maintainability.
Collaborate effectively with FDA stakeholders and REI technical leadership to deliver mission-focused solutions.
Provide strong hands-on technical guidance while supporting timely, high-quality software delivery.

Educational Qualifications:

Bachelor’s degree in Information Technology, Cybersecurity, Operations Management, or related field.

Washington, DC Metro Area — regular on-site presence at FDA facilities required, in support of account leadership and delivery oversight.

title: Senior DevOps Engineer I
description:
ABOUT ROCKET LAB

Rocket Lab is the end-to-end space company building rockets, spacecraft, and critical subsystems that keep the world connected, protected, expand humanity's reach to the Moon, Mars, and beyond. We move fast, build real hardware for meaningful missions, and make the impossible routine. Come shape the future with us.

SPACE SYSTEMS

At Rocket Lab, we're not just launching rockets — we're building the future of space. Our Space Systems team builds everything from complete spacecraft, precision payloads to the components and subsystems that allow them to thrive in space, like solar panels, flight software, star trackers, optical systems, separation systems, radios, and more.

Our Space Systems team has enabled more than 1,700 missions, ranging from interplanetary exploration, in-space manufacturing to national security and defense initiatives. The team has built spacecraft, payloads, and components for missions to the Moon and Mars, working with partners including NASA, the Space Development Agency, and the U.S. Space Force. Whether it's a single high-performance spacecraft, constellation, or the vertically integrated components that help them get to space — our world class Space Systems team is empowering some of the boldest and most ambitious space missions.

SENIOR DEVOPS ENGINEER I

Based out of Rocket Lab's site in Littleton, CO, we are looking to hire a Senior DevOps Engineer I. In this role you will build, operate, and improve the observability platform that gives our teams clear, actionable insight into the health and performance of mission-critical systems. This role sits within the DevSecOps organization and focuses on reliable, scalable telemetry collection, storage, visualization, and alerting across our environments.

This is a technical role for someone who enjoys making complex systems understandable and dependable. You will partner with Space Systems teams to improve monitoring coverage, alert quality, dashboard usability, and operational response. Your work will directly improve the reliability, performance, and security of software systems supporting space missions.

WHAT YOU'LL GET TO DO:

Build, operate, and continuously improve the organization's observability stack, including Grafana, Grafana Mimir, kube-prometheus-stack, and Grafana Alloy.
Design and maintain scalable metrics collection, ingestion, retention, and query patterns for Kubernetes and cloud-based workloads.
Develop and maintain Grafana dashboards that provide actionable insights to engineering teams and leadership.
Design, tune, and maintain alerting and notification workflows that reduce noise and enable timely, effective incident response.
Partner with engineering teams to define meaningful service-level indicators, service-level objectives, and monitoring standards.
Improve observability coverage by identifying telemetry gaps, analyzing trends, and implementing durable instrumentation and monitoring improvements.
Integrate AWS CloudWatch and CloudTrail telemetry into the observability platform to support operational visibility, security monitoring, and troubleshooting.
Manage observability infrastructure through version-controlled, automated deployments using Terraform, Git, and CI/CD pipelines.
Drive continuous improvement through data-driven analysis of platform reliability, telemetry quality, dashboard adoption, and alert effectiveness.
Troubleshoot complex monitoring, telemetry, and alerting issues across AWS, and GCP environments.
Work with development teams through code reviews and integrated pipelines to ensure observability is built in from the start.
Design and implement AI agents that detect, analyze, and troubleshoot software testing failures with minimal human intervention
Build and maintain AI-powered quality automation ecosystems that monitor CI/CD pipelines across multiple programs and platforms

YOU'LL BRING THESE QUALIFICATIONS:

Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, or other technical discipline
5+ years of experience in DevOps, site reliability engineering, platform engineering, or a related infrastructure discipline
Hands-on experience operating and improving production observability and monitoring platforms
Demonstrated expertise in AI/ML technologies with hands-on experience building AI-driven automation systems
Experience with AWS and GCP cloud services
Experience managing infrastructure as code with Terraform and collaborating through Git-based workflows
U.S. citizenship is required, due to program requirements

THESE QUALIFICATIONS WOULD BE NICE TO HAVE:

Experience with Splunk
Experience administering and configuring data visualization and analytics platforms, such as Grafana
Administration experience with Time Series Databases, such as Grafana Mimir
Strong problem-solving skills with an automation-first mindset and a track record of improving reliability in production environments
Experience deploying and managing Prometheus-based monitoring with kube-prometheus-stack
Experience configuring and operating Grafana Alloy for telemetry collection and forwarding
Strong understanding of CI/CD pipeline automation tools, DevSecOps practices, and Kubernetes operations
Experience with cloud networking concepts and troubleshooting
Experience building dashboards using tools like Grafana, Kibana, or custom visualization frameworks
Knowledge of security testing tools and DevSecOps security practices
Aerospace background supporting satellite, spacecraft, constellation, or launch vehicle ground/mission operations
Expertise in Git-based workflows, CI/CD pipelines, and Kubernetes orchestration
Experience with observability and monitoring tools
Experience with Kubecost
Operating and building solutions within GovCloud environment

This position may require prolonged periods of sitting, standing, walking, computer work, and occasional exposure to moderate levels of noise, dust, and fumes in production areas.

WHAT TO EXPECT

We're on a mission to unlock the potential of space to improve life on Earth, but that's not an easy task. It takes hard work, determination, relentless innovation, teamwork, grit, and an unwavering commitment to achieving what others often deem impossible. Our people out-think, out-work, and out-pace. We pride ourselves on having each other's backs, checking our egos at the door, and rolling up our sleeves on all tasks big and small. We thrive under pressure, work to tight deadlines, and our focus is always on how we can deliver, rather than dwelling on the challenges that stand in the way.

Ownership: We own outcomes, not just effort.

title: Principal Game AI Engineer
description:
Who We Are:

Ghost Story Games is a self-publishing game development studio founded by Ken Levine (Creative Director of System Shock 2, Bioshock, and Bioshock Infinite) and former Irrational Games developers. The studio's mission is to create narrative-driven experiences rooted in immersive world building and gameplay.

The Challenge

Ghost Story Games is seeking a talented remote Principal Game AI Engineer to join us on Judas, the highly anticipated game led by Ken Levine (System Shock 2, BioShock series). Unique in its bold, creative vision, Judas is also built upon novel technology by which the visual world, gameplay, and story unfolds in meaningful, dynamic ways. The result is a significant and personal journey adapted to each player's experience and offers a new approach to the art and storytelling of video games.

We are seeking a Principal Game AI Engineer to focus on the finalization and polish of our AI behaviors and systems. In this critical role, you will take ownership of bringing our AI systems to a "shipping-ready" state, ensuring the enemies within Judas react and behave in believable, compelling ways. Beyond technical implementation, you are expected to work closely with our design and animation teams to tune these systems and guarantee the best possible player experience.

The ideal candidate brings a proven track record of shipping games as an AI Game Engineer, pairing strong technical abilities with a deep passion for player experience.

What You'll Take On:
You will own the implementation, hardening, and polish of AI behaviors and systems to shipping quality.
You will collaborate closely with design, animation, and other disciplines to iterate on AI features, ensuring they support the creative vision and deliver an exceptional player experience.
You will ensure the quality and stability of critical AI systems, taking responsibility for delivering highly reliable behaviors.

Extensive Unreal Engine 4 and/or Unreal Engine 5 experience.
Deep experience with modern game AI architecture (Behavior Trees, pathfinding, perception systems)
Experience with modern animation techniques like root motion, distance matching, motion warping, blend spaces, and state machines
Strong knowledge of C++

Ability to quickly understand existing code and enhance/extend an existing architecture

Experience with closing down heavily dynamic and/or procedural systems.
Support build automation processes as needed.
C#/Python/Blueprint experience.

title: Security Engineer, ML Infrastructure
description:
Why work at Higgsfield AI?

Higgsfield AI is the fastest-scaling generative AI company in history, hitting $1B in annual revenue run rate, 30M+ users worldwide, 6M+ generations per day, and powering 390 of Fortune 500 brands.

We're building at the absolute frontier of AI-powered video creation and next-generation creative tools. Joining Higgsfield means becoming part of a high-impact team shaping the future of AI-native experiences, at a company that isn't just moving fast, but rewriting what fast looks like.

About the role:
Higgsfield AI is looking for a highly technical, hands-on ML Security Engineer to join Higgsfield Security and own security across our GPU clusters and AI/ML infrastructure, from model training to inference and production deployment.

In this role, you will work as part of the Security team and closely with our ML and Infrastructure teams to design, implement, and operate security controls that protect models, data, and underlying infrastructure. Your core responsibilities will include securing GPU compute environments, assessing infrastructure and AI/ML vendors, and enforcing security requirements through technical controls, deployment policies, and verified remediation.

We're looking for someone who combines deep security engineering expertise with a practical, solutions-oriented mindset. The ideal candidate is comfortable working across cloud environments, Kubernetes, Linux, and GPU infrastructure, and understands how to balance security, performance, and reliability in a fast-moving AI environment.

This role carries direct ownership of GPU infrastructure security and the security requirements that third-party providers must meet to support Higgsfield’s workloads and data.

What you'll do:
AI/ML & GPU Infrastructure Security

Own the security of GPU clusters supporting distributed training and production inference across cloud and rented datacenter environments.

Harden GPU hosts, operating systems, drivers, container runtimes, Kubernetes clusters, and workload scheduling configurations; reduce privileged access and unnecessary exposure.

Secure distributed training environments and GPU workloads through isolation, access controls, and data movement restrictions. Validate isolation between tenants and workloads across compute, networking, and storage, including shared GPU environments where applicable.

Design and implement controls to protect sensitive datasets, model checkpoints, weights, and customer data.

Strengthen inference security through tenant isolation, service authorization, secure model loading.

Partner with ML and Platform Engineering teams to integrate security into infrastructure design and development workflows.

Vendor Security Assessment & Enforcement

Lead technical security assessments of GPU infrastructure providers, datacenter operators, and other AI security vendors that process Higgsfield data and support AI workloads.

Evaluate vendor architecture and evidence covering tenant isolation, privileged access, data handling and retention, use of customer data for model training, encryption, vulnerability management, and incident response.

Translate security requirements into enforceable technical controls, including approved configurations, and continuous checks for configuration drift.

Track internal and vendor security findings to closure with accountable owners and deadlines, validate remediation, and escalate unmet requirements. Document any approved exceptions with compensating controls and expiration dates.

Cloud & Platform Security

Design, implement, and maintain security controls across Linux, Kubernetes, cloud infrastructure, networks, and third party datacenter environments.

Secure infrastructure provisioning, configuration management, and access to third-party infrastructure providers. Restrict and audit vendor and administrator access to cluster management interfaces and production systems.

Implement least-privilege access, workload identity, secrets management, encryption, and auditable access controls.

Identify and remediate vulnerabilities and configuration risks across production systems, including GPU hosts, drivers, and container runtimes, coordinating changes with infrastructure owners to maintain service reliability.

Security Operations & Risk Management

Develop and maintain detection and response capabilities for infrastructure and AI-specific security threats, including unauthorized GPU workloads, privilege escalation, and suspicious data transfers.

Investigate and respond to potential credential compromise, unauthorized data access, model theft, and compromised workloads.

Partner cross-functionally to implement practical security improvements that account for the performance, scalability, and reliability requirements of GPU workloads.

Requirements:

Strong hands-on experience in Security Engineering, Infrastructure Security, Platform Security, or a related technical discipline.

Deep understanding of Linux, Kubernetes, networking, and cloud infrastructure security.

Practical experience securing or operating GPU clusters or distributed AI/ML infrastructure, with an understanding of training and inference workloads, GPU drivers and runtimes, and workload isolation.

Experience designing and implementing security controls across complex, distributed production environments.

Strong knowledge of identity and access management, workload isolation, encryption, secrets management, and least-privilege principles.

Experience conducting technical vendor security assessments, evaluating supporting evidence, and driving remediation with external providers.

Ability to identify, investigate, and remediate security vulnerabilities and infrastructure threats.

Proficiency in scripting or programming languages such as Python, Go, or Bash.

Experience partnering with Infrastructure, Platform, or ML Engineering teams to implement security solutions.

Strong technical ownership, sound judgment, and the ability to prioritize security risks in a fast-paced environment.

A hands-on, collaborative approach with the ability to independently drive security initiatives from design through deployment, verify that controls work in production, and hold internal teams and vendors accountable for agreed security requirements.

Compensation & Benefits

We offer a competitive and thoughtfully structured compensation package designed to align with impact, experience, and long-term growth.

Base Salary: The anticipated salary range for this role is $200,000 - $300,000, depending on experience, skills, scope, and location.

• Bonus: This role is Bonus eligible and may participate in the Company's discretionary annual bonus program.

Equity: In addition to cash compensation, employees are eligible to participate in the company’s stock option program and share in Higgsfield’s long-term growth.

Benefits: We offer a comprehensive benefits package designed to support employees professionally and personally, including medical, dental, and vision insurance, a competitive 401(k) retirement plan with company matching, and additional benefits and perks.

The opportunity to work on ambitious AI products alongside a highly experienced, fast-moving, and international team.

Significant ownership, direct impact, and opportunities for professional growth as the company scales.

This is a hybrid role based in the San Francisco Bay Area. Team members are expected to work from our San Francisco office three full days per week, with the remaining days worked remotely and are expected to be available during agreed working hours and to maintain sufficient overlap with the relevant team’s time zone. We value in-person collaboration, active communication, responsiveness, and close partnership across teams.

Higgsfield AI is an equal opportunity employer. We are committed to building a diverse and inclusive team and do not discriminate on the basis of race, color, religion, sex, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, national origin, age, disability, veteran status, or any other protected characteristic.

Compensation Range: $200K - $300K

title: Forward Deployed Engineer, AI
description:
Arrowhead Pharmaceuticals, Inc. (Nasdaq ARWR) is a commercial stage biopharmaceutical company that develops medicines that treat intractable diseases by silencing the genes that cause them. Using a broad portfolio of RNA chemistries and efficient modes of delivery, Arrowhead therapies trigger the RNA interference mechanism to induce rapid, deep, and durable knockdown of target genes. RNA interference, or RNAi, is a mechanism present in living cells that inhibits the expression of a specific gene, thereby affecting the production of a specific protein. Arrowhead's RNAi-based therapeutics leverage this natural pathway of gene silencing.

Arrowhead is focused on developing innovative drugs for diseases with a genetic basis, typically characterized by the overproduction of one or more proteins that are involved with disease. The depth and versatility of our RNAi technologies enables us to potentially address conditions in virtually any therapeutic area and pursue disease targets that are not otherwise addressable by small molecules and biologics. Arrowhead is leading the field in bringing the promise of RNAi to address diseases outside of the liver, and our clinical pipeline includes disease targets in the liver and lung with a promising pipeline of preclinical candidates.

Arrowhead's corporate headquarters is in Pasadena, CA with research and development teams in Madison, WI & San Diego, CA, and a state of the art manufacturing facility in Verona, WI. Our employees are nimble, science-driven innovators who are collaborating to bring new therapies to patients in need.

The Position

This is a newly created, green-field role and the first Forward Deployed Engineer, AI hired within the company. The person in this role will partner directly with business and scientific stakeholders across multiple functions to identify high-value problems and build and deploy AI-driven solutions that solve them. Because there is no existing playbook for this function, the Forward Deployed Engineer will help define how AI solutions are scoped, built, and delivered internally, working hands-on across the AWS, Azure, Databricks, and Microsoft technology stack alongside the Data Platform Engineer, DevOps Engineer, and Databricks/AWS platform teams. This role requires someone comfortable operating with ambiguity, moving quickly from problem discovery to a working solution, and embedding directly with internal teams to understand their workflows before proposing and shipping AI tools that fit how they actually work.

Responsibilities

Partner directly with stakeholders across R&D, clinical, manufacturing, commercial, and other business functions to identify, scope, and prioritize opportunities for AI-driven internal solutions.
Design, build, and deploy agentic AI workflows and applications that solve real operational and scientific problems, working end-to-end from prototype through production.

title: GNC Engineer II, Hypersonics
description:
ABOUT FIREFLY AEROSPACE

Firefly Aerospace is a space and defense technology company that enables our world to launch, land, and operate in space – anywhere, anytime. As the partner of choice for critical space missions, Firefly is the only commercial company to launch a satellite to orbit with 24-hour notice and the only company to achieve a successful Moon landing. Our launch vehicles, lunar landers, and orbital vehicles provide government and commercial customers with full mission services from low Earth orbit to the Moon and beyond. Headquartered in north Austin, Texas, Firefly is looking for passionate, hardworking innovators to join our team and help fuel our successful trajectory into space.

SUMMARY

As a Hypersonics focused GNC Engineer at Firefly, you will design, analyze, develop, and test guidance, navigation, and control systems for advanced hypersonic flight vehicles. In this role, you will develop GNC algorithms and simulation software, perform high-fidelity trajectory and vehicle dynamics analysis, and support integration and flight test activities.

You will work across guidance, navigation, controls, aerodynamics, propulsion, flight software, and vehicle systems to develop robust GNC solutions capable of operating in highly dynamic, uncertain, and stressing flight environments. This position offers hands-on ownership of algorithms and analysis from early vehicle development through hardware-in-the-loop testing and flight operations.

RESPONSIBILITIES

Develop, implement, and validate guidance, navigation, and control algorithms for hypersonic and high-speed atmospheric flight vehicles.
Perform 6DOF modeling, simulation, and Monte Carlo analysis across nominal, dispersed, and off-nominal flight conditions.
Develop and evaluate trajectory guidance, targeting, and optimization algorithms for boost, glide, maneuvering, terminal, and other applicable flight phases.
Design and tune attitude, flight-path, and vehicle control algorithms considering aerodynamic, propulsion, actuator, and structural constraints.
Develop navigation and state-estimation algorithms incorporating IMUs, GPS/GNSS, and other vehicle sensor data.
Conduct stability, robustness, sensitivity, and uncertainty analyses across highly nonlinear and rapidly changing flight regimes.
Develop and maintain models of vehicle dynamics, aerodynamics, propulsion, sensors, actuators, atmospheric environments, and other relevant system effects.
Support software-in-the-loop (SIL), processor-in-the-loop (PIL), and hardware-in-the-loop (HIL) testing and integration of GNC algorithms with flight software and vehicle hardware.
Analyze ground and flight-test data to assess GNC performance, correlate vehicle models, identify root causes, and improve future vehicle performance.
Collaborate with aerodynamics, propulsion, structures, avionics, flight software, systems engineering, and test teams throughout the vehicle development lifecycle.

QUALIFICATIONS

Required

Bachelor’s degree in aerospace engineering, mechanical engineering, electrical engineering, physics, mathematics, computer science, or a related technical field.
2–5 years of professional experience in guidance, navigation, controls, flight dynamics, trajectory analysis, or a closely related discipline.
Strong understanding of rigid-body dynamics, flight mechanics, feedback control systems, and numerical simulation.
Experience developing or analyzing GNC systems for aerospace vehicles such as hypersonic vehicles, missiles, launch vehicles, reentry vehicles, high-performance aircraft, or other autonomous flight systems.
Experience with 3DOF and/or 6DOF vehicle simulation, Monte Carlo analysis, uncertainty propagation, and performance assessment.
Proficiency with Python, MATLAB/Simulink, or similar tools for modeling, simulation, algorithm development, and data analysis.
Familiarity with C/C++ and implementation of algorithms in embedded, real-time, or flight-critical software environments.
Understanding of software development practices including Git/version control, code reviews, testing, verification, and technical documentation.

Desired

Master’s or PhD in aerospace engineering, controls, robotics, applied mathematics, or a related field with emphasis on GNC, flight dynamics, optimization, or autonomous systems.
Direct experience developing GNC algorithms for hypersonic glide vehicles, boost-glide systems, maneuvering reentry vehicles, missiles, interceptors, or other high-speed atmospheric vehicles.
Knowledge of hypersonic flight dynamics, including aerodynamic nonlinearities, rapidly varying dynamic pressure, atmospheric uncertainty, thermal constraints, and coupled aero-propulsive effects.
Experience with trajectory optimization, optimal control, predictive guidance, nonlinear guidance, or real-time targeting techniques.
Experience with modern control techniques such as LQR/LQG, gain scheduling, nonlinear control, robust control, adaptive control, or model predictive control.
Experience with navigation and state estimation, including Kalman filtering, extended/unscented Kalman filters, inertial navigation, GPS/GNSS integration, and sensor fusion.
Experience developing aerodynamic databases or incorporating CFD, wind-tunnel, or flight-test data into vehicle simulations and GNC analysis.
Experience with SIL, PIL, HIL, real-time simulation, embedded processors, or flight-computer integration.
Familiarity with flight-test planning, test execution, telemetry analysis, and post-flight model reconstruction.
Experience working on defense programs and familiarity with development environments involving ITAR/EAR, classified systems, or U.S. Government customers.

Firefly offers outstanding benefits for our employees, including generous health, dental and vision plans with low plan deductibles, parental leave, relocation benefits, educational reimbursement, short term disability, and flexible PTO options.

To conform to U.S. Government space technology export regulations, including the International Traffic in Arms Regulations (ITAR) you must be a U.S. citizen, lawful permanent resident of the U.S., protected individual as defined by 8 U.S.C. 1324b(a)(3), or eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State.

title: Senior Signal Processing Engineer
description:
At WHOOP, we're on a mission to unlock and inspire performance for life. WHOOP empowers members to perform at a higher level through a deeper understanding of their bodies and daily lives. Our wearable technology collects rich physiological data, providing members with actionable insights into their recovery, training, and sleep.

We are seeking a Senior Sensor Algorithm Engineer to develop and deploy algorithms for physiological sensors including optical sensor and inertial measurement unit (IMU) data into accurate, reliable, and real-time insights on WHOOP devices. This hands-on role centers on digital and statistical signal processing, sensor fusion, and model-based state estimation, with a particular focus on accelerometer and gyroscope data.

You will own algorithm development from sensor characterization, mathematical modeling, and Python prototyping through efficient C/C++ implementation, firmware integration, and production validation. Working closely with Firmware, Hardware, Data Science, and Product, you will deliver robust on-device algorithms that perform reliably across diverse members and real-world conditions while meeting the constraints of wearable hardware.

RESPONSIBILITIES

Design and develop real-time signal processing and sensor fusion algorithms that combine Sensor measurements inputs to characterize motion and deliver reliable member-facing insights.

Develop and tune model-based estimators for orientation and motion, including sensor bias estimation, uncertainty propagation, and drift mitigation under changing movement and sensing conditions.

Build robust IMU processing pipelines, including filtering, calibration, time synchronization, resampling, coordinate transformations, and compensation for sensor noise and systematic errors.

Analyze large-scale, noisy wearable datasets to identify failure modes and improve robustness across motion patterns, device orientation, fit, and individual movement characteristics.

Translate algorithm prototypes into production-ready C/C++ implementations, balancing accuracy with power, memory, compute, numerical stability, and latency.

Partner with Firmware and Hardware teams on sensor configuration, sampling strategies, and on-device integration; investigate differences between prototype behavior and performance on target hardware.

Define performance metrics and rigorous validation plans using reference measurements, controlled experiments, real-world data, and on-device testing to assess accuracy, robustness, and long-duration stability.

Own technical decisions for complex algorithm components, contribute to design and code reviews, mentor teammates, and collaborate across functions to investigate post-deployment issues and drive continuous improvement.

QUALIFICATIONS

5+ years of experience developing and deploying signal processing, sensor fusion, or state-estimation algorithms for real-world sensor applications, including substantial hands-on work with IMU data.

MS or PhD in Electrical Engineering, Biomedical Engineering, Computer Science, Applied Mathematics, or a related quantitative field, or equivalent practical experience.

Strong foundation in digital and statistical signal processing, including filtering, spectral analysis, stochastic processes, and sensor noise characterization.

Demonstrated experience with accelerometer and gyroscope processing, IMU calibration, sensor error modeling, bias estimation, and drift management.

Strong experience with Kalman filtering, including extended or error-state formulations, and model-based sensor fusion; practical understanding of nonlinear estimation, uncertainty propagation, and estimator failure modes.

Practical knowledge of 3D motion and orientation representations, including coordinate frames, rotation matrices, quaternions, and rigid-body kinematics.

Proficiency in Python for algorithm development, data analysis, and experimentation, and C/C++ for efficient embedded implementation; demonstrated experience deploying algorithms to resource-constrained hardware.

Ability to independently investigate complex algorithmic problems, design rigorous validation experiments, and communicate technical tradeoffs with firmware, hardware, and cross-functional partners.

Experience with body-worn sensors, human-motion modeling, motion segmentation, or periodicity analysis is highly desirable.

This role is based in the WHOOP office located in Boston, MA. The successful candidate must be prepared to relocate if necessary to work out of the Boston, MA office.

Interested in the role, but don't meet every qualification? We encourage you to still apply! At WHOOP, we believe there is much more to a candidate than what is written on paper, and we value character as much as experience. As we continue to build a diverse and inclusive environment, we encourage anyone who is interested in this role to apply.

title: Machine Learning Engineer
description:
Company Description

Chooch helps build and run the best Computer Vision AI applications that make cameras intelligent, enhancing productivity & revenues, while reducing operational costs. Chooch has been named a leading computer vision platform by IDC.

Role Description

We are looking for a Machine Learning Engineer (US-based) to join our team. This is a full-time, hybrid role with frequent hands-on experience with customer projects in the Bay Area. The Machine Learning Engineer will be responsible for the successful design, accuracy, and backbone behind our Computer Vision AI applications. This includes data preparation, training, configuring neural networks, deploying networks in real customer locations, and refining computer vision algorithms for healthcare, manufacturing, and retail customers. This role requires frequent interaction with technical and non-technical customers while working closely within our solutions engineering teams. The Machine Learning Engineering role has opportunity to grow, lead technical projects, and improve current processes while providing meaningful feedback to our product and solutions teams.

Product Description Chooch AI is a computer vision platform that helps hospitals automate supply room monitoring and inventory management. Using fixed cameras and AI, the platform continuously tracks supplies in storage areas and updates on-hand counts in real time. When inventory levels fall below defined thresholds, replenishment orders are automatically generated and sent to ERP systems, eliminating manual counts and barcode scanning. Hospitals using Chooch AI significantly reduce critical stockouts, optimize inventory levels, and improve supply chain staff productivity. By turning supply rooms into self-managing systems, Chooch AI enables clinical and supply chain teams to focus more time on patient care.

Responsibilities/What you'll do at Chooch:

Design, train and fine-tune models for object detection, classification, segmentation, tracking and anomaly detection on real customer video and images.
Adapt pretrained and foundation models (YOLO-family detectors, ViTs, CLIP-style and vision-language models) to new customer use cases with limited labeled data.
Own data pipelines end to end: curation, labeling guidelines, augmentation, synthetic data, and dataset versioning.
Optimize models for production and edge hardware using quantization, pruning, distillation, ONNX export and TensorRT, hitting agreed latency and accuracy targets.
Build evaluation suites with clear metrics (mAP, precision/recall, false-alarm rates per camera-hour) and catch regressions before release.
Deploy and monitor models in production, diagnose drift and failure cases, and close the loop with retraining.
Work with product, solutions engineers and customers to turn vague requirements into measurable model specs.
Write clean, tested, reviewed code and contribute to shared ML tooling.

Nice to have

Experience with vision-language models (CLIP, LLaVA-style models) or open-vocabulary detection.
Multi-object tracking and video analytics (re-identification, action recognition, temporal models).
Few-shot learning, active learning, or synthetic data generation for low-data domains.
MLOps tooling: MLflow or Weights & Biases, Kubernetes, Triton Inference Server, CI/CD for models.
Domain experience in Healthcare, retail and supply chain, manufacturing inspection, workplace safety or video surveillance.

Key Components

Model Development and Optimization: Design, develop, and optimize machine learning models for computer vision applications.
Data Management: Collaborate with ML engineers to ensure the collection, processing, and maintenance of high-quality datasets necessary for model training and testing.
Algorithm Implementation: Implement state-of-the-art computer vision algorithms to improve system accuracy and performance in real-world scenarios.
Cross-Functional Collaboration: Work closely within the solutions engineering team to integrate machine learning models into the broader product and systems.
On-Site Travel and Field Testing: Many of our projects are live deployments with major fortune 500 customers – testing new, innovative ML technologies. Traveling on site is sometimes needed to see the environment, test in the real-world, and ensure the technology is operating as expected.
Performance Evaluation: Regularly evaluate the performance of computer vision models, using both qualitative and quantitative methods, and iterate to enhance accuracy and efficiency.
Research and Innovation: Understanding of the latest developments in machine learning and computer vision, applying innovative approaches and technologies to solve complex challenges.
Stakeholder Engagement: Collaborate with internal and external stakeholders to understand their needs and translate them into effective technical solutions.
Problem-Solving: Address and troubleshoot complex problems that arise during the development and deployment of computer vision systems.

The ideal candidate should be deeply passionate about machine learning and its real-world applications, particularly in improving and leveraging state-of-the-art neural networks to make an impact.

Requirements

3–5 years of industry experience building ML systems, with at least 2 years focused on computer vision.
BS or MS in Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, Math or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.
Strong Python and hands-on experience with PyTorch (or TensorFlow) for training and debugging deep learning models.
Shipped at least one computer vision model to production, and can explain the trade-offs made along the way.
Solid grasp of CNN and transformer architectures for detection, segmentation and classification.
Experience with OpenCV and image/video processing: decoding streams, preprocessing, augmentation.
Working knowledge of model optimization for inference (ONNX, TensorRT, quantization or similar).
Comfortable with Docker, Git, Linux and training on GPUs in a cloud environment (AWS/Azure).
Sound ML fundamentals: loss functions, overfitting, class imbalance, evaluation metrics and experiment design.
Clear written and verbal communication, including explaining model behavior to non-ML stakeholders.

Benefits

Chooch offers extensive benefits including health, dental, vision insurance, 401K with 3% match, extensive PTO, and life insurance policies included.

The Senior IT Engineer is a senior technical member of the global Information Technology team responsible for the administration, support, security, and continuous improvement of the company’s corporate technology environment.

This is primarily a hands-on technical position, with approximately 10–15% of the role dedicated to team coordination, operational leadership, and management responsibilities. title: Security Engineer
description:
About Ceresti

Ceresti is on a mission to reduce avoidable hospitalizations and improve care for people living with dementia while improving the lives of their families and caregivers. We envision a world in which family caregivers of people living with dementia are supported and have the knowledge, skills, and confidence to provide the best possible care for their loved ones.

Ceresti is a tech-enabled dementia care provider with a differentiated model of care that improves outcomes and delivers guaranteed cost savings by including family caregivers in the care team. We offer health plans and accountable care organizations a turnkey solution for engaging a population that has limited participation in traditional clinical programs.

Our culture is rooted in agility, innovation, and collaboration. We believe every idea—no matter how small—can spark a meaningful improvement. Together, we create solutions that make a lasting impact on the healthcare ecosystem, enabling more compassionate and cost-effective care for those who need it most.

The Role

Ceresti's engineering team is writing a lot of code. This role makes sure it is safe: threat modeled, risk evaluated, dependency-checked, and tested by someone who knows how an attacker would approach it.

The Security Engineer is the bridge between the CISO's office and Engineering. You will sit with developers, read their code, and write your own: security utility tools, automation, logging and parsing scripts, and the integrations that turn raw signal into smarter controls. Security has a front end, a back end, and a lot of scripts, and most of the work is integrating systems and automating the tooling developers already use.

You will also break things on purpose. We want someone who builds attack simulations (using AI and the tools we already run) and uses Dev, QA, and Test as a sandbox to prove where the real gaps are rather than arguing about them in the abstract.

Your main working partner is Engineering. You will occasionally build something IT runs in Microsoft 365 for example, and IT is often the end user of those tools.

What You Will Do
Secure the code Engineering writes

• Build and maintain threat models for new and existing systems and features, and keep them current as architecture changes.

• Read checked-in code and assess its security. This role reviews code; it does not only review reports about code.

• Own Snyk and Docker Scout: thresholds, findings, and driving remediation with the owning teams.

• Review the software bill of materials for outdated or vulnerable components and push fixes through to closure.

• Review SAST and DAST output, prioritize what matters, and work the remediation with engineers directly.

Write security tooling and automation

• Build security utility tools and automation that Engineering and the wider company use.

• Write scripts for logging, data parsing, and signal enrichment that make controls smarter rather than noisier.

• Integrate security systems with developer tooling so the safe path is the convenient one.

• Build and tune detection logic and automation that the Security Analyst operates day to day.

Prove the gaps are real

• Build penetration tests and attack simulations using AI and the tools we already run, and use Dev, QA, and Test as a test bed to demonstrate real exposure.

• Feed results from Pentest-Tools and internal testing back into what you build next.

• Scope, coordinate, and manage the independent third-party penetration test required for SOC 2 and HITRUST, and track findings to closure.

Shape the architecture

• Contribute to security architecture and standards, as well as detection logic.

• Represent security in engineering initiatives including the mobile app, tablet software, the data lake, and AI and machine-learning work.

• Help secure the production cloud environment (AWS via Aptible) as part of Engineering's platform, as code wherever possible.

What Success Looks Like

In the first year, we would expect to see:

• Threat models exist for the major systems and stay current as architecture changes.

• Dependency and container findings from Snyk and Docker Scout are triaged accurately and driven to closure, not just reported.

• Engineering consults you early on mobile, tablet, data lake, and AI work.

• Security tooling you wrote is in day-to-day use, and detections reach the Security Analyst with low noise.

• Attack simulations have surfaced at least one real gap that nobody had argued for on paper.

• The annual third-party penetration test is scoped, scheduled, and tracked to closure.

What You Bring
Required

• Five to seven years in software or security engineering. Not a first engineering job.

• You write code comfortably and would be at home on a development team. Python, Go, or similar.

• Hands-on application security: threat modeling, dependency and container scanning, and reading code for security flaws.

• Working knowledge of cloud security in AWS, and of CI/CD pipelines and where security fits in them.

• Offensive fundamentals: you can think like an attacker and build a test that proves a point.

• The ability to explain a finding to an engineer in terms they will act on.

Preferred

• Experience with Snyk, Docker Scout, or comparable SAST, SCA, and container tooling.

• Detection engineering: writing and tuning rules that hold up in production.

• An OSCP-type certification, or equivalent demonstrable offensive work.

• Healthcare, or another environment handling regulated data.

• Experience in a company where security was being built rather than inherited.

How you work

• You like to experiment, and you want a test bed rather than permission.

• You want help thinking through architecture, and you will ask for it. This role has room to grow into that.

• You would rather demonstrate a gap, then document it so it gets fixed.

• You treat engineers as colleagues to work alongside, not as an audience to review.

What We Offer

• Full-time remote work

• Competitive base salary with final offer based on experience, skills, and location

• Comprehensive health, dental, and vision benefits

• Equity participation in a growing healthcare technology company

• PTO and a culture that respects it

• A collaborative, mission-driven environment where your work directly supports family caregivers and improves outcomes for people living with dementia

Additional Information

Employment is contingent on successful completion of a background check, consistent with applicable law.

Ceresti is an equal opportunity employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability, veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by law.

title: Data Scientist
description:
Data Scientist

On-site in Longmont, Colorado. Monday through Friday, business hours, Mountain Time.

About Docketly

Docketly, a sister company to ABC Legal Services, is a fast-growing legal-tech company based in Longmont, Colorado. For the creditors' rights industry, we make hiring a stand-in attorney easy, fast, and reliable. We pair proprietary software with a nationwide network of attorneys.

Job Overview

You build and run the machine learning and analytics systems behind Docketly's operations. You build and run production models, from first idea to a live, monitored system on AWS. ABC Legal's data science team is your sounding board on methods. You build the BI reporting that leadership, operations, and client teams use daily. You support pricing and margin decisions with financial modeling. You work closely with backend engineers on data infrastructure and production issues. This role can grow into Senior Data Scientist as you take full ownership of the production model and the pricing roadmap.

Key Responsibilities

Model development and MLOps

Build and run the full lifecycle of production ML models: framing, feature engineering, training, validation, deployment on AWS SageMaker (Model Registry, real-time endpoints), inference infrastructure (for example, AWS Lambda), and ongoing monitoring.
Build and maintain automated retraining and drift monitoring for deployed models.
Run staged production rollouts with holdout comparisons to prove model impact before full release. Review the test design with the team before launch.
Use AI coding tools to speed up analysis, modeling, and MLOps work.

Analytics, pricing, and reporting

Build and maintain the BI layer leadership relies on for exec reporting on revenue, margin, and volume, from dashboard design through data accuracy.
Run pricing and margin analysis for client accounts, including ad hoc investigations for named strategic accounts. Model the financial impact of proposed pricing changes before they go live.
Build and maintain rules-based pricing and case-difficulty logic by court and county, alongside statistical and ML approaches.
Build and tune large scoring and prioritization frameworks in Metabase, such as weighting, percentile scenarios, and drop-rate analysis, that drive daily operational decisions such as Hearing priority and assignment.
Turn ambiguous business questions into clear, well-scoped analyses.

Cross-functional partnership and documentation

Partner with engineering on data pipelines (AWS Glue, Lambda, EventBridge). Investigate and help resolve production database performance issues, such as ORM query patterns and indexing, alongside backend engineering.
Write down your methods and decisions in Confluence or an equivalent shared space, as you go, so other teams can find your reasoning and build on it without asking you directly.

Systems & Skills

Required

Bachelor's degree in a related field, or equivalent practical experience, and 3+ years of experience with applied statistics or machine learning.

3+ years of experience with SQL and a relational database in a professional capacity. Docketly's production database runs on MySQL/Aurora, about 400 tables.

title: Senior Data Engineer
description:
About PrePass

PrePass® is North America's most trusted weigh station bypass and toll management platform. We’re transforming how the transportation industry operates—creating solutions that keep trucks moving safely, efficiently, and compliantly. This means making bold decisions and building systems that support not only fleets but the broader economy. It all starts with enabling commercial vehicles to keep rolling with seamless toll management, weigh station bypass, and safety solutions. It’s what we do best, and we do it to meet the demands of the road every day.

That’s why people join us: our solutions are implemented in real-time, on highways and interstates across the nation, helping fleets go farther, faster. This work challenges and rewards, presenting complex problems that need ambitious answers. We hire bold thinkers with a heart for impact, a passion for progress, and the optimism to shape the future of transportation.

About the Role

PrePass is seeking a Senior Data Engineer to architect, build, and scale our core data platform. In this role, you will lead the design of high-throughput data pipelines and lakehouse architectures while mentoring fellow engineers in modern software craftsmanship. We are looking for a technical leader who treats data engineering with the rigor of software engineering—relying on strict Test-Driven Development (TDD), extreme programming (XP) practices, and AI-augmented workflows to deliver reliable, observable, and mission-critical data systems in Databricks.

Key Responsibilities

Use advanced SQL, Apache Spark, and Lakehouse technologies such as Databricks and Delta Lake to support analytics, reporting, and real-time operational workloads.
Modernize Legacy Integrations: Partner with the team to define and execute a strategy for re-architecting legacy SQL Server Integration Services (SSIS) workloads into modern, cloud-native pipelines. Lead proof-of-concept and prototyping work and turn the findings into clear recommendations.
Champion TDD & XP Practices: Lead by example in writing clean, modular, and maintainable code using strict Test-Driven Development (TDD), pair programming, continuous refactoring, and automated CI/CD pipelines.
Drive AI-Augmented Engineering: Leverage AI-assisted development tools to accelerate code generation, automate unit and data-quality test creation, streamline legacy refactoring, and enhance pipeline anomaly detection.

Diagnose and resolve integration and data-quality failures, build end-to-end traceability and observability, and tune pipeline and compute performance for cost and scalability.
Elevate Engineering Standards: Define and evolve team-wide data engineering standards, architectural documentation, and continuous improvement initiatives within an Agile environment.

Requirements

Qualifications
Senior-Level Data Engineering Experience: Proven track record of designing, building, and operating distributed data pipelines and cloud data platforms at scale.
Mastery of Test-Driven Development (TDD): Demonstrated hands-on expertise in TDD for data pipelines—writing unit, integration, and data-contract tests prior to implementation—alongside XP practices such as pairing, refactoring, and continuous integration.
AI Augmentation Proficiency: Practical experience integrating AI coding assistants and LLM-based tooling into daily engineering workflows to accelerate delivery, improve test coverage, and automate documentation.
Production Operations & Observability: Strong experience operating high-availability systems in production with clear uptime, reliability, and observability expectations.
Technical Leadership: Experience driving engineering standards, architectural reviews, documentation, and mentorship within an Agile team.

Experience with Infrastructure as Code (e.g., Terraform / Bicep) for managing Databricks workspaces and cloud resources.

Databricks Expertise:Production experience with the Databricks platform (Delta Lake, PySpark/Spark SQL, Databricks Workflows, and Unity Catalog)
Background in high-volume IoT, telematics, or transportation industry data.
