title: Search & AI Discovery Architect
description:
Description:

Build your career with Heritage Auctions, the world’s largest collectibles auctioneer.

Celebrating its 50th anniversary in 2026, Heritage Auctions has spent five decades connecting collectors with extraordinary objects and the stories behind them. Headquartered in Dallas, Texas, with offices across the United States and around the world, Heritage serves more than 50 auction categories, including Coins, Sports, Comics, Entertainment, Historical, Jewelry, Fine and Decorative Art, Luxury Accessories, Wine, and many more. Join a collaborative, fast-paced company where curiosity is valued, expertise is celebrated, and every day offers an opportunity to work with remarkable pieces of history and culture.

SUMMARY:

Heritage Auctions is seeking a Search & AI Discovery Architect to make Heritage’s information easier for people and AI systems to discover, understand, trust, and cite across traditional search engines, AI-powered search, answer engines, assistants, and emerging agent ecosystems.

This role combines deep search knowledge with hands-on technical architecture and experimentation. You will own the technical designs, information and relationship models, standards, feasibility assessments, dependencies, implementation guidance, and validation that support Heritage’s search and AI-discovery strategy. You will personally build prototypes and reference implementations, then partner with Engineering to turn validated approaches into production capabilities.

As part of our Enterprise AI team, reporting to the Manager, Enterprise AI, you will work closely with the SEO and AEO Strategy Manager, who owns commercial strategy, growth priorities, the delivery backlog, and business outcomes. You will advise and influence the growth roadmap through technical evidence and emerging capabilities.

Success means making Heritage a more accessible and trusted source for auctions, collectibles, valuations, provenance, historical objects, and market intelligence while preserving the meaning and accuracy of its information. In partnership with the SEO and AEO Strategy Manager, you will support improved visibility and citations for strategic topics and a measurable contribution to qualified traffic, registrations, consignments, bidding activity, purchases, and revenue

BENEFITS:

· Medical, Dental, Vision coverage

· Paid time off

· 401k savings plans

· Onsite gym with access to a personal trainer

COMPENSATION: Commensurate on experience

LOCATION: South of Dallas/Fort Worth International Airport, NW corner of W. Airport Freeway (Hwy. 183) and Valley View Lane

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES:

• Define, document, and govern technical standards for crawlability, indexing, rendering, canonical URLs, metadata, internal linking, structured data, content architecture, and search performance. Maintain reusable implementation patterns that reduce ambiguity and repeated research. Assess how Heritage’s inventory, archives, specialist expertise, and market data are exposed to search engines and AI systems, and identify barriers to accurate discovery, retrieval, attribution, and citation.

• Develop information models, reusable schema patterns, and knowledge and relationship graphs that distinguish an object from its auction appearances, an active offering from a historical auction result, and an estimate from a realized price. Preserve provenance, relevant dates, price definitions, and reliable links between records. Work with Heritage specialists, Data Services, and Engineering to validate entity definitions, attributes, identifiers, and relationships. Validate that discovery outputs preserve these

distinctions.

• Translate business priorities into clear technical designs, requirements, dependencies, tradeoffs, and acceptance criteria for Product and Project Management, Web, Data Services, and Engineering. Provide practical implementation guidance and test cases, surface risks and unresolved dependencies early, and help resolve technical gaps through production delivery and validation against intended behavior

• Personally build prototypes and reference implementations using Heritage data to test technical approaches, expose assumptions, and demonstrate proposed standards. Run focused experiments, compare results, and iterate before recommending broader adoption.

• Evaluate APIs, data feeds, agent access, Model Context Protocol (MCP) capabilities, and emerging discovery approaches, providing practical guidance on security, data availability, feasibility, and integration. Track evolving schema practices, naming conventions, and changes in how search engines and AI agents discover and interpret information. Use experimental evidence to explain their practical implications and proactively surface capabilities and constraints that should inform or reshape planning while following agreed business priorities.

• Establish technical and discovery baselines with the SEO and AEO Strategy Manager and relevant analytics partners. Measure and validate implemented improvements for information accuracy, crawlability, index coverage, structured-data quality, and accessibility to search and AI agents. Collaborate on measurement of visibility, citations, qualified traffic, conversions, and agreed business outcomes, distinguishing technical performance from commercial results.

• In your first 90 days, work with the SEO and AEO Strategy Manager, Engineering, Data Services, Web, and Heritage specialists to establish discovery, technical-accessibility, and information-accuracy baselines for an agreed representative scope. Identify the most consequential barriers and dependencies, agree on a representative category’s information model and pilot acceptance criteria, and build and test a reference implementation. Deliver a measurable implemented pilot with Engineering and validate results against the baselines and acceptance criteria, including information accuracy and accessibility to search and AI

agents. Document results, remaining limitations, and recommendations for the next business-prioritized improvements

Requirements:

QUALIFICATIONS:

• Experience in technical SEO, web architecture, digital marketing technology, organic growth, or a related discipline, with strong knowledge of crawlability, indexing, website structure, metadata, canonicalization, and search performance.

• Broad technical understanding of front-end websites, back-end systems, structured data, APIs, data flows, and AI-discovery integrations.

• Ability to build and test prototypes and reference implementations and translate them into practical implementation guidance.

• Ability to model entities and relationships clearly and preserve the meaning of complex information across systems.

• Familiarity with AI-powered search, large language models, answer engines, and emerging discovery practices.

• Ability to translate business and marketing objectives into technical requirements and explain capabilities, constraints, and tradeoffs to technical and nontechnical partners.

• Experience partnering with developers, data engineers, product or project managers, marketers, and business stakeholders.

• Strong analytical, research, communication, and problem-solving skills, including the judgment to evaluate unfamiliar technologies and recommend a practical path forward.

• A strong sense of ownership for technical outcomes, including proactively identifying opportunities, surfacing risks, resolving gaps, and following work through validation.

PREFERRED EXPERIENCE:

• Experience implementing or guiding schema, structured-data, knowledge-graph, or entity-modeling initiatives.

• Familiarity with answer engine optimization (AEO), generative engine optimization (GEO), entity authority, or LLM visibility measurement.

• Working knowledge of JavaScript-rendered websites, content management systems, APIs, data feeds, and modern web architecture.

• Familiarity with agent integrations, MCP, or other methods for making organizational content available to external AI systems.

• Experience with Google Analytics, Google Search Console, Semrush, Ahrefs, Adobe Analytics, Salesforce, Robohead, or similar platforms.

• Experience with marketplaces, ecommerce, luxury goods, auctions, collectibles, or other expertise-driven industries

Heritage Auctions welcomes and encourages applications from women, minorities, veterans, mature workers, and persons with disabilities. EOE

title: Staff Forward Deployed Engineer, Platform
description:
Description:

About Us

eSimplicity is a modern digital services company that partners with government agencies to improve the lives and protect the well-being of all Americans, from veterans and service members to children, families, and seniors. Our engineers, designers, and strategists cut through complexity to create intuitive products and services that equip federal agencies with solutions to courageously transform today for a better tomorrow.

Purpose and Scope

We’re seeking a Staff Forward Deployed Engineer, Platform to join eSimplicity’s Rapid Innovation Center (the RIC). The Staff Forward Deployed Engineer, Platform works primarily with internal stakeholders, including program teams, growth teams, executives, business unit CTOs, security leaders, and engineering teams, to identify high-value operational and mission problems and shape the platform, DevOps, cloud, integration, and automation foundations needed to deliver working prototypes and MVPs from concept through validation.

As part of a small, high-trust team, this engineer is expected to take initiative, work effectively through ambiguity, and bring sound judgment to fast-moving technical challenges. The role requires ownership, adaptability, and close collaboration to help internal teams move quickly while establishing reliable developer workflows, secure cloud patterns, CI/CD practices, observability, infrastructure automation, and reusable platform foundations that can be adopted across the company.

The role may engage external customers when needed to understand mission context, validate assumptions, or support a program or pursuit, but its primary purpose is to help internal teams move faster and turn validated ideas into repeatable company capabilities.

This is a Staff-level, hands-on technical role for someone who can move fluidly across discovery, solution shaping, architecture, and implementation while partnering with product, program, security, and engineering leaders. This is an individual contributor role with technical leadership responsibilities; it does not include direct people-management responsibilities or ownership of companywide AI governance. Successful work is matured into repeatable patterns, reusable components, reference architectures, adoption guidance, and transition plans that other eSimplicity programs and capture teams can adopt.

Responsibilities

Partner with program teams, growth teams, executives, business unit CTOs, security leaders, engineering teams, and other internal stakeholders to identify high-value operational or mission problems, clarify needs, define success measures, and translate ambiguity into executable solution approaches.
Partner with product and design stakeholders to conduct interviews, discovery sessions, and workflow analysis, then translate those insights into user-centered concepts, interaction patterns, prototypes, and validation approaches for mission-aligned solutions.
Shape pragmatic solution approaches and contribute directly to architecture, code, integrations, demos, AI applications, data solutions, platform services, prototypes, and MVPs from discovery through validation and transition planning.
Make clear technical tradeoffs across speed, security, scalability, reuse, maintainability, cost, operational readiness, and mission value.
Design and integrate systems, APIs, data sources, cloud services, CI/CD pipelines, infrastructure-as-code, release automation, identity controls, observability, monitoring, and deployment automation using Agile, DevSecOps, DataOps, and AnalyticOps practices.
Build and evolve reusable platform capabilities, including services, APIs, developer workflows, CI/CD templates, infrastructure automation, environment patterns, data integration patterns, secure cloud patterns, and shared technical components that multiple programs and engineering teams can adopt.
Apply existing security, privacy, and responsible AI expectations appropriate to prototype or MVP maturity, including PII/PHI protection, access control, auditability, transparency, human oversight, and escalation of governance decisions to the appropriate company or program owners.
Mature successful work into reusable components, implementation patterns, reference architectures, adoption guidance, and transition plans for scaled development, sustainment, or reuse across programs and capture teams.
Enable adoption through workshops, whiteboarding sessions, onboarding materials, playbooks, technical reviews, and coaching that help internal teams understand, trust, and reuse RIC-built capabilities.
Mentor engineers, architects, and delivery teams by sharing patterns, reviewing solution approaches, and raising the technical bar across engagements.
Other duties as assigned.
Requirements:
A Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Information Systems, Engineering, Math, or a related scientific or technical discipline.
7+ years of hands-on software, data, platform, cloud, or AI engineering experience, with demonstrated ability to build solutions directly while influencing technical direction across more than one area such as discovery, solution architecture, stakeholder engagement, backlog shaping, or implementation planning.
Strong hands-on depth in platform engineering, DevOps, cloud infrastructure, CI/CD, automation, observability, identity, and secure integration patterns, with working fluency in adjacent areas such as full-stack engineering, data engineering, AI/ML engineering, or integration architecture as needed for various engagements.
Demonstrated record of taking ambiguous internal, program, or customer problems to working prototypes or MVPs quickly while maintaining sound technical judgment, security awareness, and delivery discipline.
Strong stakeholder-facing skills, including the ability to work directly with executives, program leaders, engineers, security stakeholders, capture teams, and, when needed, government customers.
Experience integrating multiple systems, APIs, data sources, cloud services, and modern AI technologies, including LLM and agentic approaches, in secure enterprise or government environments.
Experience designing and building secure solutions that handle PHI, PII, or other sensitive data, with working knowledge of privacy, authorization, governance, auditability, and responsible AI expectations.
Working knowledge of cloud services, infrastructure automation, CI/CD, build and release pipelines, identity, observability, monitoring, environment management, data integration, secure integration patterns, and reusable platform or developer-enablement capabilities.
Experience designing or operating observability practices for cloud or platform environments, including logging, metrics, tracing, dashboards, alerting, service health indicators, and operational feedback loops that improve reliability and supportability.
Excellent executive, technical, and written communication skills, including the ability to translate complex technical decisions into mission, business, delivery, and risk implications.
Experience leading work in Agile or SAFe environments, including backlog management, technical planning, delivery coordination, and use of Atlassian Jira/Confluence.
Ability to obtain and maintain a Public Trust and reside in the United States.

Preferred Qualifications

Federal, DoD, or health IT experience, especially experience influencing government stakeholders or delivering solutions in Medicare, Medicaid, healthcare, or Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services environments. GovCon experience is not required for an exceptional builder with strong stakeholder instincts.
Hands-on experience with platforms such as Databricks and Palantir, and experience designing, building, or operationalizing LLM and agentic AI applications such as MCP servers, agents, retrieval-based solutions, and governed AI workflows.
Prior forward-deployed engineering, technical consulting, solution architecture, platform engineering, or senior engineering experience, including translating prototypes into reusable components, reference architectures, and transition plans.
Experience mentoring engineers, shaping technical standards, reviewing architectures, and improving engineering quality across multiple teams or engagements.
Relevant certifications or advanced training in data platforms, cloud architecture, coding, AI/ML architecture, platform engineering, or applied AI delivery.

Working Environment:

eSimplicity supports a hybrid work environment operating within the Eastern time zone so we can work with and respond to our government clients. Expected hours are 9:00 AM to 5:00 PM Eastern unless otherwise directed by your manager.

Occasional travel for training and project meetings. It is estimated to be less than 5% per year.

Benefits:
eSimplicity offers a comprehensive benefits package, including medical, dental, and vision coverage, 401(k) retirement benefits, paid time off, paid holidays, life and disability insurance, and additional wellness and employee support programs. Eligibility may vary based on employment status and applicable plan terms.

Reasonable Accommodation:
eSimplicity is committed to providing reasonable accommodations to qualified individuals with disabilities during the application and hiring process. Applicants who need assistance or an accommodation should contact Human Resources.

Equal Employment Opportunity:
eSimplicity is an Equal Opportunity Employer, including disability and protected veteran status. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, age, protected veteran status, disability, or any other legally protected status.

title: Lead AI Architect
description:
Company Description

Domino’s is a purpose-inspired, performance-driven company powered by exceptional people who are committed to feeding the power of possible—one pizza at a time. Founded in 1960 as a single store in Ypsilanti, Michigan, Domino’s has grown into the largest pizza company in the world, with more than 22,300 stores across 90+ markets. Our success is built on the strength of our people, technology, and franchise system. As a leader in innovation, we continue to transform the pizza and QSR industry while creating opportunities for team members to learn, grow and thrive. If you're ready to make an impact, build a meaningful career and help shape what's next, there's a place for you at Domino's.

Job Description

As Lead AI Architect, you own the technical architecture for Domino's enterprise AI platform – spanning classical AI, generative AI, and agentic AI. This is the senior individual-contributor technical authority on AI: you set the direction for how AI capabilities are built, served, orchestrated, and governed, and you drive outcomes through design authority and influence rather than direct reports. You own the reference architecture and the paved road teams build on, and the build-depth judgment for every incoming ask – production now, minimum viable, scaffolded as a contract for later, or deliberately deferred rather than quietly dropped.

This is a deeply hands-on role for an architect who has delivered AI platforms and solutions at enterprise scale – someone who knows why a technique works and when it survives contact with enterprise data, latency budgets, unit economics, and governance, and who still builds prototypes and reference implementations. Our environment is Azure-primary with Databricks.

Responsibilities

Architecture Ownership and Direction

Own the enterprise AI reference architecture end to end, establishing scalable standards, principles, and design patterns across business groups.
Own the roadmap for agentic systems platforms, translating business objectives into sequenced technical strategy, milestones, and a build-depth decision for every use case with explicit, traceable reasoning.
Design and maintain the paved road for AI development – golden patterns for building, serving, evaluating, and integrating models and agents, with an API-first integration default, MCP by exception against explicit criteria, and guardrails inherited rather than bolted on per team – so teams ship without re-solving solved problems.
Guide optimization of AI compute and token usage as adoption scales, and lead build-versus-buy, model, and framework decisions with evidence – benchmarks, cost per answer, real-load latency.

Semantic Search, Retrieval and RAG Architecture

Chunking, embedding and indexing: design chunking strategy per content type and tune size, overlap, and boundaries against measured retrieval quality; select and evaluate embedding models; own re-embedding and versioning.
Query construction and hybrid retrieval: implement query rewriting, decomposition, and expansion; combine dense and sparse retrieval with fusion and re-ranking; manage the recall-versus-precision and latency trade-off explicitly.
Retrieval and response evaluation: instrument recall, precision and faithfulness against curated golden datasets; ground answers in the certified semantic layer and knowledge graphs where they outperform vector retrieval; design for graceful abstention over confident wrong answers.

Generative AI Portfolio

Define prompt and instruction management standards – versioning, templating, context budgeting, and regression testing on prompt or model changes.
Own the AI gateway and multi-model routing, matching each request to the right model on complexity, cost, latency, and quality, and own the benchmarking discipline for how models are compared, selected, and re-tested as the landscape shifts.
Establish the evaluation harness as a launch gate – offline/online evaluation, LLM-as-judge with human calibration, A/B and shadow testing, and an explicit quality threshold we won't launch below.
Hold a clear, evidence-based position on when prompt engineering suffices versus when fine-tuning or customization is warranted, and define caching strategy as a deliberate cost and latency lever.

Agentic AI Portfolio

Architect the orchestration layer that chains agents, tools, retrieval, and human review – orchestration as the enforced contract, domain agents scoped by journey and business context, and a reusable skills and tool layer where reusability actually lives.
Design memory and context management with an explicit position on what persists, for how long, and under what access rules; define enterprise standards for tool/function calling and MCP server contracts.
Establish agent guardrails – authorization scope, permission models, approval and escalation paths, sandboxing, fallback behavior, and safe failure – plus step-level tracing, regression testing, audit, and incident response.
Define the agent registry, tool catalog, memory and state services, and lifecycle from prototype to monitored production asset, and apply agentic patterns – spec-driven development, AI-assisted code and test generation – to our own engineering practice.

Governance, Trust and Security

Define responsible AI standards – bias/fairness testing, transparency, explainability, and human oversight on high-risk outputs – aligned with enterprise data governance policy rather than parallel to it.
Establish AI security patterns for prompt injection, data exfiltration, jailbreaks, and model/supply-chain risk; partner with the Data Governance team on classification, stewardship, certified sources, and access controls – Microsoft Purview, Entra ID, Unity Catalog, row-level security, PII handling, and retention.
Classify use cases by risk, drive attestation with Security, Legal, Privacy, and Risk, and lead third-party model/vendor technical review, translating findings into architecture constraints.

Observability, Economics and Platform Engineering

Instrument tracing, telemetry, and drift signals from day one so agent behavior is observable before it's questioned; build cost attribution and drive cost per successful answer as a first-class metric.
Contribute to the instrumentation that ties AI investment to measurable outcomes –partnering with platform and finance teams so unit economics are a first-class design constraint.
Define the Azure-native platform stack and lifecycle with MLOps and Engineering – Azure AI Foundry, Azure ML, AKS, model/agent registry, CI/CD, landing-zone and environment strategy, Entra ID and network patterns, capacity, and LLMOps/AgentOps for versioning, promotion, and rollback.
Partner with Engineering and Architecture teams on data readiness, certified metrics, lineage, and data contracts, and with Engineering on turning reference patterns into shipped services – defining the sanctioned builder environment so teams move fast without bypassing controls.

Technical Leadership

Raise the bar across Engineering and solution architecture through design reviews, system-level reasoning, and mentorship – driving rigor without direct reporting relationships.
Translate architecture trade-offs into clear, decision-oriented narratives for senior technology leaders and peer architects, and lead cross-team decisions with partners such as Microsoft, Databricks, strategic AI vendors, and systems integrators.
Write architecture decision records, reference patterns, and reusable accelerators, and develop proof-of-concept reference implementations that help teams move AI solutions from concept through production without rebuilding the controls.

Qualifications

Deep enterprise architecture and systems-design expertise. Proven ability to design end-to-end AI platforms spanning applications, models, data, APIs, integration, identity, infrastructure, and operations. Strong grounding in distributed systems, event-driven and service-oriented patterns, resilience, high availability, fault tolerance, and disciplined architectural decision-making.
Strong foundations in AI, machine learning, and generative AI. Deep understanding of classical ML, deep learning, NLP, foundation models, transformers, embeddings, semantic retrieval, RAG, fine-tuning, multimodal AI, and agentic or multi-agent architectures, including when to use each approach, how to weigh the trade-offs, and where each one can fail.
Data, retrieval, and knowledge architecture expertise. Ability to design structured and unstructured data ingestion, transformation pipelines, chunking and indexing strategies, vector and hybrid retrieval, knowledge graphs, metadata models, lineage, provenance, data quality, and access controls, including grounding conversational experiences in structured data (text-to-SQL, multi-turn dialogue).
Model evaluation and production lifecycle engineering. Experience establishing evaluation frameworks and benchmarks (recall@k, NDCG, groundedness, LLM-as-judge), automated testing, release controls, model and prompt versioning, observability, quality monitoring, incident response, rollback, and ongoing improvement using MLOps and LLMOps principles.
Security, privacy, responsible AI, and governance. Ability to build identity, authorization, privacy, model security, human oversight, regulatory controls, and auditability into the architecture from the start. Must understand AI-specific threats such as prompt injection, sensitive-data leakage, unsafe agent actions, and model or software supply-chain risk.
Scalability, reliability, performance, and AI economics. Ability to make quantitative architecture decisions on latency, throughput, concurrency, availability, capacity, inference architecture, compute utilization, quality-versus-performance trade-offs, consumption forecasting, and cost optimization, including AI FinOps at scale.
Business and value-oriented solution architecture. Ability to translate business strategy into qualified AI use cases, measurable outcomes, target-state architectures, investment priorities, and delivery roadmaps. Must separate value-producing opportunities from technology demos and tie solutions to operational or financial KPIs.
End-to-end delivery with hands-on technical credibility. Demonstrated ability to move from discovery and architecture through experimentation, production deployment, and operational improvement. Able to build or review prototypes (Python, SQL, Spark), validate assumptions, review implementation designs, diagnose cross-layer failures, and defend technical trade-offs, with production depth in DevSecOps, Infrastructure as Code, Kubernetes, and model serving.
Technical leadership and stakeholder influence. Experience defining reusable patterns and standards, leading architecture reviews, mentoring engineers and architects, and aligning product, data science, engineering, infrastructure, security, and business teams. Creates clarity in ambiguity, leads with integrity and humility, and communicates well with executives and practitioners alike.
Substantial enterprise AI delivery experience. A strong record of leading complex AI or ML solutions in production at enterprise scale, typically 10+ years across software, data, or ML engineering with significant architecture leadership.

Preferred Qualifications

Hands-on experience with Microsoft environment: Azure (AI Foundry and Agent Service, Azure OpenAI, Azure ML, AI Search, API Management, Functions), Databricks and Copilot Studio; agent frameworks such as LangGraph or Semantic Kernel and MCP.
Experience in retail, restaurant, e-commerce, or supply chain with high-volume, real-time workloads and streaming (Kafka, Event Hubs) and model risk management.
Production multi-agent systems and agent runtimes, policy-aware agent gateways with authenticated tool routing and server registries, and GPU-accelerated serving stacks.
Contributions to open-source AI projects, published work, or recognized community involvement.

Additional Information

Benefits:

Paid Holidays and Vacation
Medical, Dental & Vision benefits that start on the first day of employment
No-cost mental health support for employee and dependents
Childcare tuition discounts
No-cost fitness, nutrition, and wellness programs
Fertility benefits
Adoption assistance
401k matching contributions
15% off the purchase price of stock
Company bonus

All your information will be kept confidential according to EEO guidelines.

title: GenAI Fullstack Engineer
description:
Marlabs, a global AI and Digital Solutions Consulting firm, delivers intelligent solutions across AI, data, analytics, and product engineering. Since 2000, we have partnered with some of the largest healthcare, life sciences, financial services, and government organizations worldwide. As we continue to expand our global footprint, we have an exciting opportunity for a highly skilled GenAI Fullstack Engineer to join our innovative and dynamic team.

This position requires onsite 5 days/week

GenAI Fullstack Engineer | About the Role

As a GenAI Fullstack Engineer, you will design and build scalable enterprise applications that combine robust Java-based backend engineering with modern Generative AI capabilities. You will work across Java, Spring Boot, Microservices, Python, FastAPI, LLMs, RAG, and Vector Databases to develop production-ready AI services and integrate them with enterprise applications. The ideal candidate is a strong software engineer who has expanded into hands-on GenAI engineering and can develop secure, scalable solutions spanning traditional backend services, AI orchestration, enterprise knowledge retrieval, and LLM-powered applications.

GenAI Fullstack Engineer | Day-to-Day

Design, develop, and maintain scalable backend applications and REST APIs using Java, Spring Boot, Microservices, Spring Security, and Spring Data/JPA.
Build and integrate production-grade GenAI and LLM applications, connecting AI services with existing Java/Spring Boot enterprise applications and business systems.
Design and implement Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) pipelines, including document ingestion, chunking, embeddings, indexing, semantic search, context retrieval, reranking, and response generation.
Develop AI services and orchestration components using Python and FastAPI, leveraging frameworks such as LangChain, LangGraph, LlamaIndex, or Hugging Face to support reusable enterprise AI capabilities.
Implement and optimize Vector Databases such as Pinecone, Weaviate, OpenSearch, FAISS, or ChromaDB to enable enterprise knowledge retrieval and semantic search.
Integrate LLM platforms such as Azure OpenAI, OpenAI, AWS Bedrock, Claude, Gemini, or Llama, applying prompt engineering, response evaluation, guardrails, and optimization techniques to improve solution accuracy and reliability.
Build secure and observable AI/backend services by implementing authentication, authorization, exception handling, logging, monitoring, API security, and production-grade engineering standards.
Containerize and deploy applications using Docker and CI/CD pipelines, collaborating with architects, data engineers, developers, and business teams to deliver reliable and scalable GenAI solutions.

GenAI Fullstack Engineer | Skills & Experience

Strong software engineering 3+ years experience with Java, Spring Boot, Microservices, and REST APIs, including hands-on experience designing scalable and distributed enterprise backend applications.
Hands-on experience developing production GenAI/LLM applications, including LLM integration, prompt engineering, response evaluation, and enterprise AI use cases.
Strong production experience with RAG architectures, including embeddings, document ingestion, chunking, semantic retrieval, reranking, context construction, and RAG quality optimization.
Strong working knowledge of Python and FastAPI, with experience building AI/ML services and integrating Python-based AI components with Java/Spring Boot applications.

title: Security Engineer, ML Infrastructure
description:
Why work at Higgsfield AI?

Higgsfield AI is the fastest-scaling generative AI company in history, hitting $1B in annual revenue run rate, 30M+ users worldwide, 6M+ generations per day, and powering 390 of Fortune 500 brands.

We're building at the absolute frontier of AI-powered video creation and next-generation creative tools. Joining Higgsfield means becoming part of a high-impact team shaping the future of AI-native experiences, at a company that isn't just moving fast, but rewriting what fast looks like.

About the role:
Higgsfield AI is looking for a highly technical, hands-on ML Security Engineer to join Higgsfield Security and own security across our GPU clusters and AI/ML infrastructure, from model training to inference and production deployment.

In this role, you will work as part of the Security team and closely with our ML and Infrastructure teams to design, implement, and operate security controls that protect models, data, and underlying infrastructure. Your core responsibilities will include securing GPU compute environments, assessing infrastructure and AI/ML vendors, and enforcing security requirements through technical controls, deployment policies, and verified remediation.

We're looking for someone who combines deep security engineering expertise with a practical, solutions-oriented mindset. The ideal candidate is comfortable working across cloud environments, Kubernetes, Linux, and GPU infrastructure, and understands how to balance security, performance, and reliability in a fast-moving AI environment.

This role carries direct ownership of GPU infrastructure security and the security requirements that third-party providers must meet to support Higgsfield’s workloads and data.

What you'll do:
AI/ML & GPU Infrastructure Security

Own the security of GPU clusters supporting distributed training and production inference across cloud and rented datacenter environments.

Harden GPU hosts, operating systems, drivers, container runtimes, Kubernetes clusters, and workload scheduling configurations; reduce privileged access and unnecessary exposure.

Secure distributed training environments and GPU workloads through isolation, access controls, and data movement restrictions. Validate isolation between tenants and workloads across compute, networking, and storage, including shared GPU environments where applicable.

Design and implement controls to protect sensitive datasets, model checkpoints, weights, and customer data.

Strengthen inference security through tenant isolation, service authorization, secure model loading.

Partner with ML and Platform Engineering teams to integrate security into infrastructure design and development workflows.

Vendor Security Assessment & Enforcement

Lead technical security assessments of GPU infrastructure providers, datacenter operators, and other AI security vendors that process Higgsfield data and support AI workloads.

Evaluate vendor architecture and evidence covering tenant isolation, privileged access, data handling and retention, use of customer data for model training, encryption, vulnerability management, and incident response.

Translate security requirements into enforceable technical controls, including approved configurations, and continuous checks for configuration drift.

Track internal and vendor security findings to closure with accountable owners and deadlines, validate remediation, and escalate unmet requirements. Document any approved exceptions with compensating controls and expiration dates.

Cloud & Platform Security

Design, implement, and maintain security controls across Linux, Kubernetes, cloud infrastructure, networks, and third party datacenter environments.

Secure infrastructure provisioning, configuration management, and access to third-party infrastructure providers. Restrict and audit vendor and administrator access to cluster management interfaces and production systems.

Implement least-privilege access, workload identity, secrets management, encryption, and auditable access controls.

Identify and remediate vulnerabilities and configuration risks across production systems, including GPU hosts, drivers, and container runtimes, coordinating changes with infrastructure owners to maintain service reliability.

Security Operations & Risk Management

Develop and maintain detection and response capabilities for infrastructure and AI-specific security threats, including unauthorized GPU workloads, privilege escalation, and suspicious data transfers.

Investigate and respond to potential credential compromise, unauthorized data access, model theft, and compromised workloads.

Partner cross-functionally to implement practical security improvements that account for the performance, scalability, and reliability requirements of GPU workloads.

Requirements:

Strong hands-on experience in Security Engineering, Infrastructure Security, Platform Security, or a related technical discipline.

Deep understanding of Linux, Kubernetes, networking, and cloud infrastructure security.

Practical experience securing or operating GPU clusters or distributed AI/ML infrastructure, with an understanding of training and inference workloads, GPU drivers and runtimes, and workload isolation.

Experience designing and implementing security controls across complex, distributed production environments.

Strong knowledge of identity and access management, workload isolation, encryption, secrets management, and least-privilege principles.

Experience conducting technical vendor security assessments, evaluating supporting evidence, and driving remediation with external providers.

Ability to identify, investigate, and remediate security vulnerabilities and infrastructure threats.

Proficiency in scripting or programming languages such as Python, Go, or Bash.

Experience partnering with Infrastructure, Platform, or ML Engineering teams to implement security solutions.

Strong technical ownership, sound judgment, and the ability to prioritize security risks in a fast-paced environment.

A hands-on, collaborative approach with the ability to independently drive security initiatives from design through deployment, verify that controls work in production, and hold internal teams and vendors accountable for agreed security requirements.

title: Forward Deployed Engineer, AI
description:
Arrowhead Pharmaceuticals, Inc. (Nasdaq ARWR) is a commercial stage biopharmaceutical company that develops medicines that treat intractable diseases by silencing the genes that cause them. Using a broad portfolio of RNA chemistries and efficient modes of delivery, Arrowhead therapies trigger the RNA interference mechanism to induce rapid, deep, and durable knockdown of target genes. RNA interference, or RNAi, is a mechanism present in living cells that inhibits the expression of a specific gene, thereby affecting the production of a specific protein. Arrowhead's RNAi-based therapeutics leverage this natural pathway of gene silencing.

Arrowhead is focused on developing innovative drugs for diseases with a genetic basis, typically characterized by the overproduction of one or more proteins that are involved with disease. The depth and versatility of our RNAi technologies enables us to potentially address conditions in virtually any therapeutic area and pursue disease targets that are not otherwise addressable by small molecules and biologics. Arrowhead is leading the field in bringing the promise of RNAi to address diseases outside of the liver, and our clinical pipeline includes disease targets in the liver and lung with a promising pipeline of preclinical candidates.

Arrowhead's corporate headquarters is in Pasadena, CA with research and development teams in Madison, WI & San Diego, CA, and a state of the art manufacturing facility in Verona, WI. Our employees are nimble, science-driven innovators who are collaborating to bring new therapies to patients in need.

The Position

This is a newly created, green-field role and the first Forward Deployed Engineer, AI hired within the company. The person in this role will partner directly with business and scientific stakeholders across multiple functions to identify high-value problems and build and deploy AI-driven solutions that solve them. Because there is no existing playbook for this function, the Forward Deployed Engineer will help define how AI solutions are scoped, built, and delivered internally, working hands-on across the AWS, Azure, Databricks, and Microsoft technology stack alongside the Data Platform Engineer, DevOps Engineer, and Databricks/AWS platform teams. This role requires someone comfortable operating with ambiguity, moving quickly from problem discovery to a working solution, and embedding directly with internal teams to understand their workflows before proposing and shipping AI tools that fit how they actually work.

Responsibilities

Partner directly with stakeholders across R&D, clinical, manufacturing, commercial, and other business functions to identify, scope, and prioritize opportunities for AI-driven internal solutions.
Design, build, and deploy agentic AI workflows and applications that solve real operational and scientific problems, working end-to-end from prototype through production.
Establish foundational engineering practices, standards, and reusable patterns for AI solution delivery, since this is the first role of its kind in the organization.
Work closely with the Data Platform Engineer to access, model, and productionize data needed for AI solutions across Databricks and AWS.
Collaborate with the DevOps Engineer to build reliable CI/CD pipelines, deployment processes, and monitoring for AI applications across AWS/ Databricks inside a MS environments.
Leverage the Databricks platform and AWS services (e.g., Bedrock, Lambda, S3) to build and orchestrate agentic AI workflows and applications, primarily by composing and integrating existing foundation models rather than training new ones.
Integrate solutions with Microsoft/Azure tools (e.g., Azure AI services, M365) where appropriate to meet business needs.
Rapidly prototype proof-of-concepts with internal teams, gather feedback, and iterate quickly to move validated solutions into production.
Document architecture, decisions, and delivery patterns to build a repeatable internal playbook for future forward-deployed engineering work.
Act as a hands-on technical resource embedded with business teams, translating ambiguous business problems into concrete technical solutions.

Requirements

Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Engineering, Data Science, or a related technical field, or equivalent practical experience.
5+ years of professional software engineering experience, including building and deploying production-grade applications.
Hands-on experience with AWS cloud services and Azure/Microsoft cloud services.
Experience working with Databricks, including data engineering, notebooks, and/or ML workflows.
Strong proficiency in at least one modern programming language (e.g., Python, SQL, or similar) used for building data and AI applications.
Demonstrated experience building agentic workflows and applications with generative AI and LLM-based approaches (e.g., orchestration frameworks, tool use, retrieval-augmented generation) to solve practical business problems.
Proven ability to work independently in ambiguous, undefined environments and to build solutions from the ground up without an established playbook.
Strong cross-functional communication skills, with the ability to translate technical concepts for non-technical business stakeholders and vice versa.

Preferred

Knowledge of the pharmaceutical, biotech, or life sciences industry is desirable but not required.
Experience with Databricks certifications, AWS certifications, or Microsoft Azure certifications.
Prior experience in a "forward deployed engineer," solutions engineering, or embedded engineering role, working directly with business teams rather than in a purely centralized product function.
Experience with LLMOps/agent-ops tooling and practices for deploying, monitoring, and evaluating agentic workflows in production.
Familiarity with regulated-industry considerations (e.g., data privacy, validation, GxP) relevant to deploying AI solutions in a pharma environment.
Experience building internal tools, chatbots, or agentic AI applications using modern LLM frameworks.
A builder mindset with the initiative to define scope and process in a green-field function.

Arrowhead provides competitive salaries and an excellent benefit package.

Candidates must have current, valid authorization to work in the country where this role is located.

title: Network and Data Center Facility Engineer
description:
Chamberlain Group (CG) is a global leader in intelligent access and Blackstone portfolio company. Powered by our myQ technology, we make access simple and secure for millions of homeowners, businesses, and communities worldwide. Our flagship brands, LiftMaster® and Chamberlain® , are found in 51+ million homes, and 14 million+ people rely on the myQ® app daily.

The Network and Data Center Facilities Engineer ensures the reliability, efficiency, and operational integrity of the physical infrastructure supporting CGI’s IT and manufacturing environments. Responsibilities include managing power distribution, CRAC units, HVAC systems, structured cabling, and environmental controls across three primary data centers and a manufacturing plant. This role supports uptime, safety, compliance, continuous improvement, and sustainability while partnering with IT, manufacturing, and facilities teams to align infrastructure operations with business needs.

Job Responsibilities:

Manage and maintain power systems—including UPS, PDUs, generators, and switchgear—across data centers, warehouse distribution centers, and manufacturing sites, including facilities in Mexico.
Oversee CRAC and HVAC systems to maintain optimal cooling and environmental conditions for IT equipment.
Use BMS and DCIM tools to monitor and respond to environmental alerts, including temperature, humidity, and airflow.
Lead preventive and corrective maintenance programs for facility infrastructure.
Coordinate vendors and contractors for equipment service, upgrades, and emergency repairs.
Ensure compliance with applicable safety, electrical, and environmental regulations, including NFPA, OSHA, and ASHRAE standards.
Create and maintain documentation, including schematics, SOPs, site rack elevations, and maintenance logs.
Support capacity planning and infrastructure scaling for new deployments and expansions across U.S. and international sites.
Participate in disaster recovery planning and execution to ensure facility readiness.
Partner with IT teams to align physical infrastructure with network and server requirements and support rack-and-stack activities across global sites.
Collaborate with IT teams to support network and server decommissioning, upgrades, and related infrastructure changes across global sites.
Provide 24/7 on-call support for critical facility incidents.
Lead audits and inspections and implement corrective actions as needed.
Advance energy-efficiency and sustainability initiatives across facilities.
Select vendors for UPS, PDU, generator, and switchgear maintenance and installation across U.S. and Mexico sites.
Develop RFPs for new installations of structured cabling, UPS, PDUs, generators, and switchgear.
Mentor junior technicians and support staff.
Assist network and server teams with device and server installations while managing cabling and fiber administration in data centers in accordance with Chamberlain and ANSI/BICSI standards.
Support access point installations across facilities.
Oversee external colocation spaces through quarterly vendor reviews focused on uptime and critical maintenance records.
Comply with health and safety guidelines and rules; managers should also ensure compliance across their teams.
Protect Chamberlain Group’s reputation by keeping information confidential.
Maintain professional and technical knowledge by attending educational workshops, reading professional publications, establishing personal networks, and participating in professional societies.
Contribute to the team effort by accomplishing related results and participating on projects as needed.

Job Requirements:

Bachelor’s degree in electrical engineering, Facilities Management, or related field, or equivalent experience.
6-8+ years of experience in LAN/WAN environments installing managing and troubleshooting multiple sites, managing a NOC environment.
6 -8+ Years managing data center or industrial facility infrastructure.
Proven experience with power systems, HVAC, and CRAC unit.
Experience in coordinating with IT and manufacturing teams.

Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities:

Strong understanding of electrical and mechanical systems.
Knowledge of NFPA, OSHA, ASHRAE standards.
Excellent troubleshooting and incident response skills.
Strong project management and vendor coordination abilities.
Proficient in documentation and reporting tools.
Ability to work in high-pressure, mission-critical environments.
NVIDIA AI certification: AI Infrastructure and Operations Fundamentals.
Generative AI Bootcamp.
Claude 101 Workshops INTL.
Familiarity with BMS, DCIM, and environmental monitoring tools.

Other:

Able to travel between sites (As required).
Availability for after-hours support and emergency response

Preferred Job Requirements:

Certified Data Center Management Professional (CDCMP), PMP, or equivalent.
Experience managing multi-site data center operations.
Experience with sustainability and energy efficiency programs.

Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities:

Familiarity with ITIL and infrastructure lifecycle management.
Familiarity with hybrid IT environments and edge computing infrastructure

The pay range for this position is $75,900.00 - $144,525.00; base pay offered may vary depending on a number of factors including, but not limited to, the position offered, location, education, training, and/or experience. In addition to base pay, also offered is a comprehensive benefits package and 401k contribution (all benefits are subject to eligibility requirements). title: AI App Lead
description:
Confiz is seeking an AI App Lead in Denver, CO. As the AI Lead you own both the architecture and the hands-on delivery of AI-powered applications built on Databricks, Python, and React. You set technical direction for a team of data, ML, and full-stack engineers while still writing production code yourself.

You will design LLM, RAG, and agentic systems on the Databricks Lakehouse, expose them through Python services, and deliver them to users through React front ends. You build secure, scalable, cost-efficient production solutions, and you are accountable for making sure the code matches the architecture.

Responsibilities

Leads the end-to-end architecture of AI solutions, including LLM applications, RAG pipelines, and agentic workflows, from data ingestion to the user interface.
Designs and builds data and ML pipelines on Databricks using Delta Lake, Unity Catalog, MLflow, Databricks Workflows, and Mosaic AI (Model Serving, Vector Search, Agent Framework).
Builds and reviews production Python services (FastAPI or similar) that expose models, retrieval, and agents through secure, well-documented REST APIs.
Architects and contributes to React (TypeScript) front ends for AI experiences, such as chat interfaces, streaming responses, source citations, and human-in-the-loop review screens.
Selects LLM providers and models (e.g., Databricks-hosted foundation models, Azure OpenAI, Anthropic) and retrieval options based on quality, latency, cost, and data-governance fit.
Establishes LLMOps and MLOps practices: model and prompt versioning, automated evaluation, tracing, monitoring, drift detection, and retraining.
Produces architecture and design artifacts for complex AI applications and is accountable for ensuring the delivered code meets them.
Leads code and architecture reviews, and mentors engineers on RAG, agent design, prompt engineering, and evaluation.
Ensures solutions meet security, privacy, and compliance standards, including Unity Catalog access controls, PII handling, guardrails, audit trails, and responsible AI practices.
Identifies and automates fixes for recurring issues to improve the operational stability and cost efficiency of AI workloads.
Translates business requirements into technical architecture in partnership with product owners and stakeholders, clearly communicating trade-offs to both technical and non-technical audiences.

Requirements

10+ years of software engineering experience, including 3+ years designing and delivering AI/ML systems in production and hands-on work with generative AI.
Demonstrated experience leading engineers and setting technical direction, while remaining hands-on in code.
Advanced Python: production services, async programming, testing, packaging, and PySpark.
Hands-on Databricks Lakehouse experience: Delta Lake, Unity Catalog, MLflow, Databricks Workflows, and Spark-based processing; experience with Model Serving and Vector Search.
Strong React with TypeScript: component architecture, state management, API integration, and streaming or real-time UIs.
Deep understanding of LLMs, RAG architectures, agentic systems, prompt engineering, LLM evaluation, and model fine-tuning.
Proven experience designing scalable distributed systems, REST APIs, and microservices, with a solid grasp of system design and security principles.
Strong SQL, data modeling, ETL/ELT pipeline design, and data governance.
Experience with Azure, AWS, or GCP AI and data services.
Hands-on infrastructure-as-code experience (Terraform, Bicep, or CloudFormation), including Databricks Asset Bundles (DABs) for versioning and deploying jobs, pipelines, and model serving endpoints through CI/CD.
Proficient in CI/CD, Git, automated testing, and the full software development life cycle.
Strong stakeholder communication: able to translate architecture into business value for technical and non-technical audiences.

Nice to Have

Databricks certifications, such as Generative AI Engineer Associate, Machine Learning Professional, or Data Engineer Professional.
Experience with agent and orchestration frameworks (LangGraph, LangChain, LlamaIndex, DSPy) and the Model Context Protocol (MCP).
Experience with vector databases beyond Databricks Vector Search, such as Pinecone, Weaviate, or pgvector.
Exposure to Docker and Kubernetes.
Experience with Next.js, design systems, and accessible UI development.
Prior experience in client-facing, pre-sales, or solutioning capacity.
Experience in a regulated industry such as financial services.

We have a global team of amazing individuals working on highly innovative enterprise projects & products. Our customer base includes Fortune 100 retail and CPG companies, leading store chains, fast growth fintech, and multiple Silicon Valley startups.

What makes Confiz stand out is our focus on processes and culture. Confiz is ISO 9001:2015 (QMS), ISO 27001:2022 (ISMS), ISO 20000-1:2018 (ITSM) and ISO 14001:2015 (EMS) Certified. We have a vibrant culture of learning via collaboration and making workplace fun.

People who work with us work with cutting-edge technologies while contributing success to the company as well as to themselves.

To know more about Confiz Limited, visit https://www.linkedin.com/company/confiz/

title: AI Data Operation Lead, Autonomy
description:
Rivian Autonomy is seeking an AI Data Operation Lead to lead the people and processes that turn vehicle data into reliable training and evaluation datasets. Within the AI Platform organization, you will bring together labeling delivery, data quality, curation, and human review to support the development of our autonomous driving models.

You will lead internal teams and external partners, with accountability for delivery, quality, and cost. This includes making sure the data we send for annotation is usable, that accepted labels meet the model teams' requirements, and that reviewers can turn difficult driving events into actionable feedback for engineering.

You will work closely with Perception, Planning, Data Infrastructure, Eval Infrastructure, and Product to translate model-development priorities into operational plans and provide evidence for release decisions. We are looking for a leader who can develop managers and specialists, make clear tradeoffs when demand exceeds capacity, and build an operation that improves as our models, tools, and vehicle fleet evolve.

Lead the organization. Set the operating plan for AI data operations, develop team leaders, and define responsibilities across employees, contractors, and vendors. Build capacity plans that account for annotation, quality review, and rework across concurrent programs.
Deliver data that model teams can use. Translate training and evaluation needs into labeling specifications, reviewer guidance, delivery milestones, and acceptance criteria. Work with model teams on taxonomy changes and keep delivery aligned with their development cycles.
Improve data quality and yield. Own the operational checks that determine whether collected vehicle data is ready for curation and labeling. Partner with collection and engineering teams to resolve sensor, calibration, and data-quality issues before they consume downstream annotation capacity.
Own vendor performance and spend. Set service levels and quality expectations, evaluate suppliers, and manage capacity, pricing, and budgets with Finance and Procurement. Reconcile accepted work with invoices and address delivery or quality shortfalls through clear corrective actions.
Develop human evaluation and triage operations. Build review workflows with autonomy and systems engineers to investigate driving events, classify recurring failures, and assemble the evidence needed for root-cause analysis. Feed those findings into scenario selection, evaluation datasets, and targeted data requests.
Run the operation with consistent metrics. Establish a shared view of accepted-data volume, quality, turnaround time, backlog, rework, collection yield, and cost. Use these measures to identify constraints, allocate review capacity, and make delivery commitments teams can plan around.
Improve tools and automation. Partner with Data Infrastructure, Eval Infrastructure, and Applied General AI on labeling tools, prelabels, automated quality checks, and assisted triage. Define operational requirements and validate improvements against measured quality and reviewer effort before scaling them.

10+ years leading operations, including at least 5 years supporting autonomous vehicles, robotics, or complex machine-learning programs, with responsibility for budgets or a P&L.
Experience managing annotation partners across domestic and international locations, including commercial negotiations, staffing plans, and service delivery.
Enough technical depth in AI development to discuss data requirements and failure analysis with engineers and turn those discussions into clear work for operations teams.
A record of developing managers and specialists, establishing ownership, and adapting team structures as priorities change.
Strong analytical judgment: you can separate a quality problem from a capacity or tooling problem, test the cause, and follow through on the fix.
Clear communication across engineering, product, finance, and operations, with the ability to make prioritization decisions and explain their impact on delivery.

Bonus Points

Direct experience supporting autonomous driving or other physical AI systems through data production and evaluation.
Experience applying large language models, multimodal models, or generative AI to annotation and human-review workflows.

title: Lead Backend Engineer – DPS Core & Data Engine Squad
description:
Salary range is:

$119,030.52 - $165,000.00

This position is bonus and/or commission eligible.

CCC Intelligent Solutions Inc. (CCC) is a leading cloud platform for the multi-trillion-dollar insurance economy, creating intelligent experiences for insurers, repairers, automakers, part suppliers, and more. At CCC, we’re making life just work by empowering more than 35,000 businesses with industry-leading technology to get drivers back on the road and to health quickly and seamlessly. We’re pushing boundaries with innovative AI solutions that simplify and enhance the claims and repair journey. Through purposeful innovation and the strength of its connections, CCC technologies empower the people and industry relied upon to keep lives moving forward when it matters most. The Role
We are seeking a Lead Backend Engineer who is passionate about database modernization, performance optimization, and strategic refactoring of mission-critical systems. You will be a key member of the DPS Core & Data Engine Squad, working on the system-of-record platform that powers both internal (DPS) and external (IES) claims management experiences supporting millions of transactions and billions of dollars in claims.

This is a modernization engineering role for someone who gets excited about:
• Refactoring complex stored procedures and carving out domain logic into maintainable services
• Optimizing SQL performance and improving system efficiency
• Creating safe migration patterns that enable continuous modernization while maintaining business continuity
• Working in .NET codebases and evolving them into clean, testable, domain-aligned modules

Database Engineering & Modernization (60%)

Performance engineering: Query tuning, indexing strategy, execution plan analysis, optimizing data access patterns

Advanced query optimization (execution plans, index tuning, query hints)

Database design and normalization

Performance tuning at scale (multi-million row tables, complex joins, aggregations)

Understanding of indexing strategies (clustered, non-clustered, filtered, columnstore)

SQL Agent jobs and automated workflow patterns

Transaction isolation levels, locking, and concurrency management

C# and .NET Framework/.NET Core (legacy and modern)

SQL source control (migrations, version control for schema/stored procedures)

Experience with strangler fig, anti-corruption layer, and facade patterns in practice

Familiarity with domain-driven design (DDD) concepts (bounded contexts, aggregates, repositories)

Observability tools (Application Insights, SQL Profiler)

API design and versioning (REST, OpenAPI/Swagger)

Unit testing frameworks (xUnit, NUnit) and test data builder patterns

PowerShell for database scripting/automation

Experience with microservices architecture and event-driven patterns

Familiarity with Entity Framework Core, Dapper, or other ORMs (and knowing when to use native SQL)

title: Design Engineer - Built World
description:
About Build

AI for the Built World: Build has created the agentic AI stack for institutional real estate, automating complex development and acquisitions workflows 90% faster than humans to accelerate the world's most important built projects - digital infrastructure, energy, industrial - from concept to completion.

Our mission is to accelerate and amplify the world's most important built projects - inventing a better way to build through a collaboration between human experts and agentic AI. We envision a future where the world's buildings are driven from concept to completion, autonomously. Without delays, cost, and complexity. Enabling people to deliver a magnitude more deals. To make decisions, build relationships and create.

To start, we're partnering with the world's biggest built world institutions from $T alternative assets investors, prolific developers and even governments to push the frontier of what's possible. We're backed by c-suite from Blackstone and OpenAI alongside the world's best venture capital firms.

Join us in shaping the future of the Built World and exponentially accelerate your career in the process. We welcome you to do your life's work here.

About the role

This role exists to make sure Build designs the way the best engineers do. The Design Engineer brings an engineering lens to data centers, power and energy infrastructure, and the wider built environment, and takes projects through design: from concept and feasibility to a coordinated, buildable scheme.

You are the source of truth for how a project actually gets engineered when the loads are large, the timelines are tight and the stakes are high.

You can expect to:

Take live projects through design: site and capacity studies, concept design, MEP, electrical and mechanical systems, and critical facilities design.

Size and lay out power, cooling and resilience systems for data centers and energy infrastructure, and pressure-test them against cost, schedule and constructability.

Work alongside Build's domain experts and engineers to turn design judgment into workflows, rules and checks that can be encoded into software.

Run proofs-of-concept for new design workflows by doing the work yourself, with an engineer supporting you on Build's systems.

Own design quality from an engineering perspective. If an output wouldn't survive review by a serious design firm, it's your job to surface and fix it.

Act as a credible peer to developers, operators, utilities and design consultants, speaking their language.

Feed what you learn on projects back into the core product.

What we're looking for

Hands-on design experience on data centers, mission-critical facilities, or power and energy infrastructure.

Strong grounding in MEP: electrical distribution, mechanical and cooling systems, redundancy (N+1, 2N) and critical facilities design.

Experience at a leading engineering or design firm (e.g. Arup, Jacobs, Burns & McDonnell, Corgan, HDR, Syska Hennessy), or on a hyperscaler or colocation design team.

Taken projects from concept through detailed design, coordinating across disciplines and with contractors.

Comfortable with numbers and tools: load calcs, single-line diagrams, BIM/Revit, and spreadsheets or scripts to move fast.

Bias to ownership and speed. You'd rather ship a working answer today than a perfect one next month.

Nice to haves

PE licence (or on track), or chartered engineer status.

Exposure to utility interconnection, on-site generation, BESS or grid-scale energy projects.

Experience with design automation, generative design, or scripting (Python, Dynamo, Grasshopper).

A degree in mechanical, electrical or civil engineering, or architectural engineering.

How to win at Build

Growing Build requires a radically different approach to company building. As a company we're focused on one outcome: winning. That means we move fast, work with intensity, and demand excellence from ourselves. We operate with intensity but create an environment that allows for a lot of fun together. The result is that we're one of the fastest shipping teams in vertical AI, partnering with the best to automate the world around us.

Performance and teamwork are the core of Build's operation. We look for those who are able to do both, who often exhibit a particular ability for;

Velocity: You are relentless in asking the right questions to set direction. Once you find the right direction you go all-in.

Excellence: You obsess with being the best. For you, excellence is a non-negotiable standard rather than an aspiration.

Long time horizons: You choose to be in something for the long run, because that's where most of the returns are realized.

Ownership: You take full ownership of the outcomes. You're meticulous in your pursuits and believe you can actively shape your environment rather than adapt to it.

Customers: You have a passion for the built world and those who shape it. You probably have a quirky hobby or story that relates to your love for building.

Integrity: You chose to do the right thing even when it isn't easy.

Trust: You only work with people you can trust because it's the only way to do truly extraordinary things.

Yield: You have a burning need to see a result on every action you take and you're always looking for routes to do more with less.

What we offer

Radical autonomy, real ownership: High standards. Minimal bureaucracy. You own problems end-to-end, choose how the work gets done, and are accountable for exceptional outcomes. Ownership is matched with meaningful, generous equity.

An accelerated founder's track: Build is for builders. If you want to learn what it actually takes to create a generational company - Product judgment, execution speed, and accountability - there is no faster path than building from zero when everything is for grabs.

Elite teammates, uncompromising bar: You work with people who think clearly, execute relentlessly, and take full ownership. The team you build becomes the company you build. Growth here is not just professional; it reshapes how you operate and in return how Build operates.

Perpetual adventure: We attract the strongest of the strange. Extraordinary experiences are part of the culture - from the food we eat together to the space we occupy. Intensity is intentional.

Shape the built world: We are rebuilding how the physical world gets made. Our software doesn't live in the abstract - it turns into real projects breaking ground because we exist. We work with the largest institutions, push the frontier of AI, and watch our decisions translate directly into the world around us.

Compensation Range: $150K - $220K

title: Search & AI Discovery Architect
description:
Description:

Build your career with Heritage Auctions, the world’s largest collectibles auctioneer.

Celebrating its 50th anniversary in 2026, Heritage Auctions has spent five decades connecting collectors with extraordinary objects and the stories behind them. Headquartered in Dallas, Texas, with offices across the United States and around the world, Heritage serves more than 50 auction categories, including Coins, Sports, Comics, Entertainment, Historical, Jewelry, Fine and Decorative Art, Luxury Accessories, Wine, and many more. Join a collaborative, fast-paced company where curiosity is valued, expertise is celebrated, and every day offers an opportunity to work with remarkable pieces of history and culture.

SUMMARY:

Heritage Auctions is seeking a Search & AI Discovery Architect to make Heritage’s information easier for people and AI systems to discover, understand, trust, and cite across traditional search engines, AI-powered search, answer engines, assistants, and emerging agent ecosystems.

This role combines deep search knowledge with hands-on technical architecture and experimentation. You will own the technical designs, information and relationship models, standards, feasibility assessments, dependencies, implementation guidance, and validation that support Heritage’s search and AI-discovery strategy. You will personally build prototypes and reference implementations, then partner with Engineering to turn validated approaches into production capabilities.

As part of our Enterprise AI team, reporting to the Manager, Enterprise AI, you will work closely with the SEO and AEO Strategy Manager, who owns commercial strategy, growth priorities, the delivery backlog, and business outcomes. You will advise and influence the growth roadmap through technical evidence and emerging capabilities.

Success means making Heritage a more accessible and trusted source for auctions, collectibles, valuations, provenance, historical objects, and market intelligence while preserving the meaning and accuracy of its information. In partnership with the SEO and AEO Strategy Manager, you will support improved visibility and citations for strategic topics and a measurable contribution to qualified traffic, registrations, consignments, bidding activity, purchases, and revenue

BENEFITS:

· Medical, Dental, Vision coverage

· Paid time off

· 401k savings plans

· Onsite gym with access to a personal trainer

COMPENSATION: Commensurate on experience

LOCATION: South of Dallas/Fort Worth International Airport, NW corner of W. Airport Freeway (Hwy. 183) and Valley View Lane

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES:

• Define, document, and govern technical standards for crawlability, indexing, rendering, canonical URLs, metadata, internal linking, structured data, content architecture, and search performance. Maintain reusable implementation patterns that reduce ambiguity and repeated research. Assess how Heritage’s inventory, archives, specialist expertise, and market data are exposed to search engines and AI systems, and identify barriers to accurate discovery, retrieval, attribution, and citation.

• Develop information models, reusable schema patterns, and knowledge and relationship graphs that distinguish an object from its auction appearances, an active offering from a historical auction result, and an estimate from a realized price. Preserve provenance, relevant dates, price definitions, and reliable links between records. Work with Heritage specialists, Data Services, and Engineering to validate entity definitions, attributes, identifiers, and relationships. Validate that discovery outputs preserve these

distinctions.

• Translate business priorities into clear technical designs, requirements, dependencies, tradeoffs, and acceptance criteria for Product and Project Management, Web, Data Services, and Engineering. Provide practical implementation guidance and test cases, surface risks and unresolved dependencies early, and help resolve technical gaps through production delivery and validation against intended behavior

description:

At RevStar, we build cutting-edge cloud, data, and Generative AI solutions that transform how enterprise organizations operate. As an Advanced AWS Consulting Partner, we don’t just deliver code—we solve complex business problems, modernize legacy infrastructure, and deploy production-grade cloud native and AI applications that drive real business value. We are seeking a Data & AI Forward Deployed Engineer (FDE) to join our Digital Solutions Practice. You will own the full delivery lifecycle for high-impact enterprise accounts—architecting resilient cloud-native environments, modernizing legacy infrastructure, and deploying state-of-the-art AWS Generative AI (Amazon Bedrock, Q, SageMaker) architectures. AWS Generative AI & Machine Learning: Architect and deploy enterprise GenAI and ML workloads leveraging Amazon Bedrock, SageMaker, Vector Databases (OpenSearch, Pinecone, pgvector), and custom RAG implementations.
